The CEO opens the Agents view expecting to staff their company, sees a 92-role org, tries to hire — and gets a dropdown of 4 roles whose entire work-product is a markdown file and a passive notification (customagents.py:51,153-171). That's the moment 'indistinguishable from a real multi-billion-dollar company' dies

The CEO asks the visa/tax advisor a real question with money on the line; the charter promises named-source, date-checked citations, but no eval, no reviewer, and no verification ever checks a single claim before it lands in their feed — the first confidently wrong fee or deadline is the last question they ask

Week 4: the same builder ships the same category of bug it shipped in week 1, and the 'org' shows zero sign of having learned — a human employee would have been managed out; an AI employer that can't learn confirms every skeptic's prior

A board member's technical diligence reads factory.py and finds the launch-blocking code review runs on Haiku while the code was written by Opus (factory.py:1527 vs 96) — the review theater unravels the entire 'FAANG-grade process' pitch in one file

The CEO messages their 'Backend Engineer' expecting the accountable owner described in its charter and gets a cold-spawned amnesiac that has never seen their company, their prior builds, or its own definition of done

The CEO's 'daily digest' tells every tenant, every day, 'real paying users: 0 — no product is deployed/sold yet' plus a hardcoded hot-take about pomodoro apps, regardless of their actual business (digest.py:88,93-94) — instant credibility death.
Tenant A opens Approvals and sees tenant B's hire requests and dead-task error messages — and can approve tenant B's hires (approvals.py:97-112,216-219). One screenshot of that kills the acquisition.

A CEO blows 100% of their token budget with zero warning because forecast's alert sweep — the file's entire reason to exist — was never scheduled; the wall the docstring promised to prevent is exactly what they hit.

The CEO reviews the plan and types 'this does not look good' — _affirmative (loopcontroller.py:1239) matches '\bgood\b', the gate clears, and a paid build fires against the rejected plan. Same for "don't do it", 'I am not ready yet', 'far from perfect' (verified by running the regex).

At the prototype gate the CEO says 'change the pricing page to annual billing' — gets 'Got it — I'll fold that in.' (loopcontroller.py:711), then says 'approve', and IMPLEMENT builds the original stored plan verbatim; the instruction was acknowledged and discarded.

The CEO's 'daily brief' — if anyone ever scheduled it — opens with 'real paying users: 0 — no product is deployed/sold yet' and a canned riff on pomodoro apps (digest.py:87-94) regardless of what their business is; and it arrives on the developer's phone, not theirs.

Every event lands as URGENT (loopcontroller._ping defaults, line 226) — options ready, prototype ready, overrun warning, ship — so within a day the bell means nothing and the one real emergency drowns.

An agent needs the CEO to 'approve this charge' via askuser.ask(); the surfacing hook is a swallowed try/except (askuser.py:52-57), no notification fires, no deadline exists — the loop waits forever and the CEO never knows they were asked.
A security-critical urgent for tenant #83,000 pages the founder's personal ntfy phone (notifications.py:87) while the tenant themself gets a print() to stdout because emailer.py doesn't exist.

…except it wouldn't even pause, because the appguard sweep is on no schedule — so in the OTHER failure mode a runaway app quietly bleeds money for hours because the circuit-breaker never runs until someone manually invokes it.

The CEO opens docs/QA-REPORT.md to check what was verified before LAUNCH and a diligent one discovers it's the platform's own canned golden artifact (controller.py _seed writes gate_check._REAL_QA) — instant, unrecoverable trust collapse for a user who already trusts AI less than humans.

The CEO pauses mid-typing on a form in their shipped product and a leaked timer bounces them — the exact bug class STANDARDS-qa.md documents as having reached the owner, still untestable because no product QA path types at human pace or dwells.

A frustrated user churns on Monday over an onboarding dead-end; the acceptance dogfood pass that would flag it runs the following week, as a curl-based text audit, under a persona rotation that is stuck on 'first-run' because the selftest polluted the audit counter.

verdicts.mechanism: Console shell: single-file server + string-concat SPA (nav, routing, polling)
verdicts.why: The entire product UI for 100k CEOs is one Python BaseHTTPRequestHandler serving a single inline HTML string (console.py:464-1392) with innerHTML-built views. There is ZERO URL routing — no pushState/hash anywhere (grep: 0 hits), so the browser back button exits the app, refresh loses your place, and nothing is deep-linkable or shareable. Views update by 5-6s/15s setInterval polls (console.py:1000,1376-1377), not push. Inline-style hacks like style=margin:6px_0 (console.py:1005,1016,1076) are invalid CSS that silently drops the margin — visible slop in the orgs/agents/agentic tiles. ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1 with a synchronous psycopg connect per request is a dev toy, not a commercial front end.
verdicts.action: Rebuild the front-of-house as a real SPA (any modern framework) with URL routing, server push (SSE/WebSocket) for live state, and an API server that isn't http.server. Keep the JSON view-module contract — it's the one salvageable layer.

verdicts.mechanism: Assistant / controller chat (streaming, first-run wizard, options/plan cards)
verdicts.why: Genuinely the best-crafted surface: SSE token streaming with blocking fallback (console.py:1220-1250, 1411-1471), saved-idea persistence across the provider gate (console.py:905-931), option/plan/design review cards (console.py:1172-1200). But it is ONE flat thread per company with a single anonymous 'assistant' — no named agents, no delegation ('ask the CTO', '@security'), no parallel workstreams. The live-progress ETA is a HARDCODED table (_PHASE_ETA_MIN, console.py:163-164) — 'IMPLEMENT: 14 min' — and when it's wrong the bubble says 'taking a little longer than usual' forever (console.py:216-217,225-226). North star says every decision is agentic, not hardcoded; a CEO staring at a fake countdown that never resolves is a churn moment. assistant.py (the org=0 home router) doesn't even exist yet — org=0 silently falls back to the first company (console.py:111-127).
verdicts.action: Keep the streaming/gate UX. Replace the flat thread with a multi-thread inbox of named agents (per project/department), make ETAs come from the controller's real plan, and ship assistant.py so 'All companies' is a real account-wide brain, not a fallback.

verdicts.mechanism: Cockpit (company at a glance: KPIs, health, projects, comms, queue)
verdicts.why: It is an honest tenant-scoped rollup (cockpit.py:110-152) with a plain-language verdict line (cockpit.py:244-306) — good bones. But the 'company' is a build queue: a hardcoded 5-stage pipeline PIPELINE=['SPEC','BUILD','QA','REVIEW','LAUNCH'] (cockpit.py:37), products shown as machine slugs like 'abc123-app' (console.py:363-364 generates them), and 'Communications' is a 15-row table of truncated intents (cockpit.py:123-127) with NO way to read what any agent actually said. comms_graph() — the one thing that could make the org feel alive — is fully implemented server-side (cockpit.py:309-338) and NEVER fetched by the frontend (grep '/api/comms_graph' in the PAGE JS: 0). The view issues ~8 sequential awaited fetches per render (console.py:1037-1043). No revenue, no users, no customer signal — a CEO of a multi-billion-dollar company sees token counts.
verdicts.action: Render the comms graph and make every communication clickable through to the full conversation. Replace stage bars with a live activity narrative ('QA found 3 issues, builder is fixing #2'). Add business KPIs (users, revenue, uptime of shipped products) next to spend. Batch the fetches into one payload.

verdicts.mechanism: Org visibility (orgview.py org chart + console 'Org chart'/Team view)
verdicts.why: The north star is 'elastic recursive orgs... tens of thousands of employees'. The actual org chart is a STATIC Python list of 9 roles, one level deep, all reporting to 'controller' (orgview.py:35-45), overlaid with a 15-minute liveness window. The console renders it as two flat card lists ('Controller' + 'Reports', console.py:1103-1107) — not even a tree. The Team view shows a 'Seats' table containing your own tenant id as the only member plus the literal string 'Multi-seat RBAC is on the roadmap (Team tier).' shipped to the user (console.py:352, 1102). A skeptical CEO opens 'Org chart' expecting a living company and finds nine hardcoded job titles and a roadmap apology — this is the single biggest illusion-break in the product.
verdicts.action: Build a real dynamic org: agents as first-class entities with names, tenure, current assignment, history and reporting lines derived from actual spawn/delegation data; a zoomable tree/graph that grows as the controller hires; click any agent to see their work and message them. Delete the static ORG list and the 'roadmap' copy.

verdicts.why: Broken by a field-name mismatch — the classic declared-not-wired bug: designview.gallery() returns html / html_excerpt / preview_text (designview.py:73-84), but the console looks for s.image||s.thumbnail||s.screenshot, s.preview_url||s.url and s.preview_html (console.py:1021-1023) — none exist. Result: every prototype card renders title + status + 'Approve design' with NO preview. The CEO is asked to approve designs they literally cannot see — a trust-killer at the exact moment the product should astonish. Worse, the dead preview_html branch injects raw HTML into the console DOM unsandboxed (console.py:1023) — if ever wired as-is, agent-generated HTML executes in the console origin (stored XSS by design).
verdicts.action: Wire the real fields: render gallery html in a sandboxed iframe srcdoc, show preview_text as fallback, add side-by-side compare and request-changes with a comment (not just approve/back-to-draft).

verdicts.why: change_plan() is 'intentionally money-free' — it flips a DB column with no payment (billingview.py:57-75), and the UI tells the user so: 'Real payment is gated (BYO Stripe).' (console.py:1093). The commercial bar (hundreds of millions, hundreds of thousands of paying users) is unreachable with zero payment rails. The topbar spend chip logic is broken-by-inspection: it builds '$' + (tokens!=null ? invoice.total : '') and needs a second fallback when it renders a bare '$' (console.py:884-885). Usage is shown as raw token counts — meaningless to a CEO. No invoice history, no receipts, no per-company cost allocation.
verdicts.action: Integrate a real payment provider (Stripe subscriptions + metered usage), show cost per company/project in dollars with trends, and rewrite the topbar chip to one deliberate format.

verdicts.why: Sixteen hardcoded catalog entries where connect() for 'oauth' items (Stripe, GitHub, Slack, Salesforce, Google Analytics) performs NO oauth — it just writes status='connected' with no credential and no verification (integrationsview.py:101-120). The console collects api_key secrets via a NATIVE BROWSER prompt(): "prompt('API key / secret for '+slug+' (leave blank if OAuth):')" (console.py:1333). So a CEO 'connects' Salesforce, sees a green 'connected' pill, and nothing works — the system lied. For a user base that already distrusts AI, a fake green checkmark is fatal. Compare: the Providers view right next to it does real validated key entry (console.py:1339-1358) — the team knows how, this surface just never got it.
verdicts.action: Real OAuth flows per provider, validated key entry using the Providers-view pattern, a post-connect verification ping ('we listed your 3 Slack channels'), and per-integration health status. Never show 'connected' without a verified credential.

verdicts.why: crossorgview.py is honest and tenant-scoped (portfolio/analytics/failures, crossorgview.py:67-167), but 'everything across all your companies' amounts to a 5-column table of counts and one success-rate percentage. No revenue per company, no trend lines, no comparative performance, no drill-down. The cross-org OPS layer (steal_feature proposals, /api/xorg + /api/xorg/propose, console.py:414,446) has ZERO frontend callers (grep: 0) — the most CEO-like capability in the codebase (make my companies learn from each other) is invisible. crossorgview.analytics/failures are polled in the portfolio view but recommendations() (crossorgview.py:170-176) is never surfaced.
verdicts.action: Wire /api/xorg into the Portfolio view as a real 'cross-company moves' panel (propose/approve feature transfers), add per-company sparklines and recommendations, and put the portfolio verdict line at the top of the org=0 home.

verdicts.mechanism: Notifications, briefings and escalation (notifications view + digest.py)
verdicts.why: North star bullet #1 is 'The CEO is briefed'. There is no briefing anywhere in the tenant product. notifications.py is a flat feed with prefs; email is a stub that print()s when no emailer is configured (notifications.py:61-69) and the 'push' pref column drives nothing tenant-facing. digest.py — the one real 'founder's digest' — is platform-operator-only (portfolio.py P&L, ntfy to the owner's phone), not tenant-scoped, not in the console. 'Mark all read' fires one POST per notification in a loop (console.py:1296). The feed has no grouping, no 'while you were away', no priority triage beyond a level pill. A CEO returns after a weekend and gets a raw reverse-chron list.
verdicts.action: Build a tenant-scoped daily/weekly CEO brief (what shipped, what's blocked, decisions waiting, spend vs plan, recommended next moves) rendered as the org=0 home landing AND delivered via email/push. Add a bulk-read endpoint.

verdicts.why: The concept (consent, hire_request, dead_letter, blocked_build in one inbox) is right, but the console's decide() is fire-and-forget: await post(...); go('approvals') — errors are swallowed silently and the item just... stays (console.py:1332). Decisions carry a one-line 'detail' string with no attached evidence: no diff, no cost impact, no agent's argument for/against, no link to the artifact being approved. A real CEO approval comes with a memo; this is a button next to a sentence. There is also no notion of 'consulted on the calls that matter' — no thresholds, no delegation rules ('auto-approve hires under $X').
verdicts.action: Attach full context to each approval (artifact link, cost, the requesting agent's rationale, what happens on deny), surface decide() failures inline, and add CEO-settable auto-approval policies so the inbox only contains calls that genuinely matter.

verdicts.why: traceview implements runs() and a step-by-step replay() (traceview.py:102-138) — exactly the 'watch your org work' feature — and the frontend never calls either (/api/runs, /api/replay: 0 callers). Same for /api/project detail, /api/versions + rollback, /api/budgets, /api/quality/product (all 0 callers) — snapshot/rollback and per-project budget caps are fully built server-side and unreachable by any user. Four whole views (fleet, observability, chat, build) exist in VIEWS but appear in no NAV entry and no go() call (console.py:691-695 vs 947+) — dead code shipped in the page. The Activity view shows raw error snippets as <code> to a CEO (console.py:1087) with no triage narrative. This is the memory-noted 'declared-not-wired' bug-class at product scale.
verdicts.action: Wire project detail (click a project → stages, versions, budget, quality verdict, run replay in one screen), delete the four dead views, and translate errors into incident narratives ('QA caught a failing checkout test; builder is on fix #2') instead of stack snippets.

verdicts.why: The guided first-run (save-the-idea, checklist parity between Assistant and Cockpit, console.py:905-931, 1046-1057) is thoughtfully engineered. But step 2 shatters the fantasy: 'Connect an AI model' requires the CEO to bring their own Anthropic/OpenAI key or run a CLI login that 'connects the whole machine to one account — ideal for a self-hosted, single-operator setup' (console.py:1131, shipped verbatim in the Technical details). A skeptical first-time user is asked to fetch API keys before seeing ANY magic. There is no demo company, no pre-provisioned trial inference, nothing astonishing before the paywall-shaped chore. The hero promises 'Be the CEO of a company of AI agents' (console.py:585) and the first task is DevOps.
verdicts.action: Ship platform-provided trial inference (metered free tier) so the first build starts within 60 seconds of signup, and/or an interactive demo company with live agents visible pre-signup. Move BYO-key to a cost-saving option, never a gate.

missing: A CEO briefing of any kind in the tenant product — no morning brief, no 'while you were away', no weekly review; digest.py exists but is operator-only ntfy, never tenant-scoped or in the console (north star bullet #1 is entirely absent)
Any real-time feel: no WebSocket/SSE for views (only the one chat stream); the 'living org' is 5-15s polling of tables — no activity ticker, no agents visibly working, no motion

Delegation ergonomics beyond one chat thread: cannot message a specific agent/role, no @-mention, no task assignment, no 'ask my CTO'; dashboard.py has two-way agent messaging but it is operator-only and token-gated
Business KPIs: no revenue, users, growth, or product-health metrics anywhere tenant-facing — the CEO of 'multi-billion-dollar companies' sees only token spend and build counts
URL routing / deep links / browser history — nothing in the app is linkable or navigable with back/forward
Multi-seat and roles: single-owner only, with 'RBAC is on the roadmap' shipped as UI copy (console.py:352)
Human-pattern comms: no status reports, no disagreement/escalation threads, no post-mortems or incident narratives surfaced to the CEO (incident.py exists backend-side, unwired)
Scale affordances: nothing handles or conveys more than ~5 products / ~9 agents — no search, no command palette, no pagination, no aggregation for '10,000s of employees'
Real payments (Stripe checkout/metering) — plans switch by flipping a DB column
Mobile/notification delivery for the tenant: push pref exists in settings but no tenant push channel; email is a print() stub without an emailer
Demo/trial magic before the BYO-key gate — nothing astonishes a skeptic in the first 5 minutes
Real OAuth for the 5+ integrations labeled 'oauth' in the catalog

Opening 'Org chart' to meet your company and finding 9 hardcoded job titles in a flat list plus 'Multi-seat RBAC is on the roadmap (Team tier).' (orgview.py:35-45, console.py:352)

The Design phase asks you to APPROVE screens that render with no preview at all — the console reads fields (image/preview_url/preview_html) the backend never returns (console.py:1021-1023 vs designview.py:73-84)

Clicking Connect on Stripe/Salesforce pops a native browser prompt() for a secret, then shows a green 'connected' pill without validating anything — the first discovered lie ends the relationship (console.py:1333, integrationsview.py:101-120)
The progress bubble promises 'about 14 min left' from a hardcoded table, then degrades to 'taking a little longer than usual — still working' with no ceiling, forever (console.py:163-164, 216-217)
Pressing the browser back button exits the app; refreshing loses your place; nothing is shareable — no routing exists (grep pushState/hash: 0 hits)

full.headline: We promised the cockpit of a multi-billion-dollar AI conglomerate and shipped a competently-plumbed localhost admin panel: one chat thread, nine hardcoded employees, design approvals you can't see, integrations that lie about connecting, and not a single briefing — no skeptic pays for this, let alone nine figures.

full.domain: Orchestration / intelligence core — loopcontroller.py, scripts/orchestra/* (actor.py, bus.py, supervisor.py, org_decider.py, orchestra.py), factory.py, project.py, orchestrator.py, dispatcher.py, fleet.py

verdicts.mechanism: loopcontroller.py — the live product brain (one durable state machine per org: DISCOVER->...->DELIVER)
verdicts.why: This is the ONLY orchestration actually wired to the console (console.py:44,142), and it is the literal opposite of 'every decision agentic'. The next-action layer is a fixed 9-phase waterfall (loopcontroller.py:42-43) whose every decision is regex, not AI: _affirmative (1236-1241) matches bare \bgood\b, \bready\b, \bdo it\b — a CEO typing 'hmm, that's not good' or 'ready in what sense?' at the approval gate (say():706-710, 641-644) silently APPROVES a build; _is_status_query (1244-1250), _intent_auto_proceed (1253-1264) and _option_ordinal (1267-1285) are more regex gates on multi-thousand-dollar decisions. One product lifecycle per company: thread_for_org returns the single thread (393-402), and after DELIVER the phase never resets — say() falls through to a generic 'Answer the CEO briefly' LLM turn (721-722), so 'great, now build the mobile app' can never build again. RUNNING_TIMEOUT_MIN=30 (993) reaps any still-'running' job as crashed (1056-1065); only research returns the 'pending' sentinel — a healthy 35-minute IMPLEMENT/qualityloop build is falsely declared failed to the CEO, and when it actually finishes the guarded terminal write (365-370) discards the successful result. Jobs are daemon threads in whatever process called say() (374), so an API-server restart drops in-flight work until the scheduler sweep. Context is a 12-turn window (1176) — the controller of a 'multi-billion-dollar company' has goldfish memory. The ops hygiene (durable controller_jobs, SLA watchdog 1086-1145, honest live status 267-302, pending_intent queueing 599-621) is genuinely good and should survive.
verdicts.action: Keep the durability substrate (controller_jobs, live-status, SLA watchdog, gates) and replace the decision layer wholesale: an agentic controller (the orchestra Controller pattern, for real) that holds the company's persistent state/memory, decides next action / escalation / notification via model calls, classifies CEO intent with the model (kill every regex intent gate), supports many concurrent workstreams per company and a continuous post-ship life (v2s, ops, incidents), and distinguishes 'job is slow' from 'worker is dead' by heartbeat instead of a flat 30-min guillotine.

verdicts.mechanism: scripts/orchestra/* — the 'new event-driven actor core' (actor.py, bus.py, supervisor.py, orchestra.py)
verdicts.why: It is a parallel toy, full stop. grep across the entire repo: NOTHING outside scripts/orchestra imports any of it — zero production callers; orchestra.py's only entry points are 'selftest' and 'demo' (orchestra.py:432-438), and the demo's 'AI decisions' are a canned stub storyline of hardcoded JSON strings (_make_demo_agent, orchestra.py:287-336). Worse, it is THREE redundant, mutually incompatible actor implementations: actor.py+bus.py (LocalBus/MessageBus, dict messages, JSON directives), supervisor.py (its own Bus/Event/Actor/Worker/Supervisor), and orchestra.py (TeamWorker/TeamSupervisor subclasses). The 'durable' Postgres bus (bus.py) is explicitly NOT used by the orchestra controller — it runs on supervisor.py's in-memory deque 'because it makes the demo deterministic' (orchestra.py:10-12). The reactor is single-threaded: Bus.pump (supervisor.py:94-104) delivers events one at a time and Worker.act() makes its AI call INLINE — the 'elastic recursive org' executes one agent at a time, serially. All org state lives in Python objects; a crash loses the entire company. No tenancy, no consent/provider/budget gates, no cancellation, no UI surface. actor.py._ai reads r.get('out') — the tail-truncated 1500-char preview (actor.py:240) — the exact truncation bug loopcontroller documents fixing at :1203-1206. Base Supervisor._escalate marks the blocked child done (supervisor.py:356-358) so an escalated worker is silently collapsed for aggregation instead of parked-and-resumed (only the demo subclass fixes this).
verdicts.action: Build ONE durable actor runtime instead of three demos: actors and org trees as Postgres rows (like controller_jobs), events on the persisted bus, real parallel execution (the existing task queue + worker pool), all factory gates enforced per actor, resumable across process death — and make it THE engine loopcontroller dispatches into. Delete the other two implementations.
verdicts.files: scripts/orchestra/orchestra.py:10-12,287-336,432-438; scripts/orchestra/supervisor.py:69-104,356-358; scripts/orchestra/actor.py:240; scripts/orchestra/bus.py (unused by its own controller)

verdicts.why: The one place where org shape IS a real AI decision — and it is called by nobody. should_expand ('called at EVERY decision point', org_decider.py:9-14) has ZERO callers anywhere in the repo; plan_org is called only by the unwired orchestra.py demo. So the north star's 'org expansion is an intelligent AI decision' exists as a well-tested library function that the product never consults. Its bias-to-expand-on-ambiguity default (129-162) means an unparseable model reply spawns MORE paid agents by design ('cost is NOT a constraint', :95) — directly contradicting the tenant-billed, budget-governed reality of factory.py:480-506 it would run inside. The prompt-and-normalize engineering itself is solid.
verdicts.action: Wire it: loopcontroller/project should call plan_org to shape the build org from the vision, and supervisors should call should_expand on live signals (blocked children, backlog) — with the expansion decision made budget-aware (pass the tenant's remaining budget as a signal) instead of pretending cost doesn't exist.

verdicts.why: agent() is the best code in the domain: layered gates (governance spawn, consent, provider, budget, killswitch, token governor, factory.py:410-506), retry/backoff, Codex failover (599-620), BYO-key routing, light/fast path — a real governed primitive. But the build 'process' around it is a hardcoded script, not an org: SPEC->BUILD->DESIGN->QA->REVIEW is a fixed function with fixed roles and fixed prompts (1358-1466+), verdicts parsed by string-matching 'CRAFT: PASS' out of a markdown tail (1458-1462), and rework bounded by MAX_FIX=3 (:90) regardless of stakes. No AI ever decides WHICH stages, roles, or rigor a given product needs. And the scale ceiling is a single Python semaphore: _AGENT_SEM = BoundedSemaphore(AOS_MAX_AGENTS=8) (:94) caps ALL agents for ALL tenants on one box — CEO #2's company queues behind CEO #1's build. The out/out_full truncation trap (587-591) has now bitten two separate callers (orchestrator.py:181, actor.py:240) after being fixed once in loopcontroller — the API design invites the bug.
verdicts.action: Keep agent() as the governed primitive. Make the line agentic: a planner decides the stage graph/roles/rigor per product (the org_decider pattern), verdicts returned as structured JSON not magic strings, per-tenant concurrency quotas instead of one global semaphore, and rename/remove tail-truncated 'out' so no future caller can parse the wrong field.

verdicts.mechanism: project.py — build_complex, the recursive multi-component engine
verdicts.why: The most credible 'complex things' capability in the repo: architect->DAG with interface contracts, cycle validation (77-105), recursion via decompose (361-369), parallel exploration + judge (199-225), component-level resume (240-245), fail-closed verification (396-408). But it is exactly the fan-out->wait-for-ALL barrier model the orchestra blueprint declares obsolete: hard 'BARRIER between layers' (:372) means one slow/stuck component stalls the entire layer; a blocked component just returns a blocker string upward (291-292) — no escalation, no resolution, no resume, the run simply ends BLOCKED_AT_COMPONENTS and the CEO gets 'retry or tell me what to change'. Shape is hardcoded: '4-8 components' in the architect prompt (:143), MAX_DEPTH=2 (:46), 5 workers (:371). It builds Python-only products ('ONE Python codebase', :142) — a 'YouTube competitor' org that can only emit stdlib Python is a punchline.
verdicts.action: Fold it into the (real) actor runtime: components as actors under a supervisor so a blocker escalates and resumes instead of killing the run; let the architect (not env vars) decide depth/width/stack; drop the layer barrier for dependency-triggered starts.

verdicts.mechanism: orchestrator.py — the second chat brain (clarify->propose->confirm quick-build)
verdicts.why: A duplicate, weaker brain living beside loopcontroller — same consent/provider gates, same [[BLOCK]] parsing, its own confirm path — which docs/blueprint/REDESIGN-unified-controller.md:50 already sentences to demotion, yet it still ships. It reads the tail-truncated r.get('out') (orchestrator.py:181), the exact bug loopcontroller documents at :1203-1206: a reply over 1500 chars can lose text (and the front of a large [[BUILD]] block), silently degrading proposals. It replays the ENTIRE thread history into every turn with no window (:174), and _run_and_report's outcome messaging is fire-and-forget daemon threads (:275) with none of loopcontroller's durable-job recovery — a process restart eats the report and the CEO never hears back.
verdicts.action: Execute the REDESIGN doc: keep chat_messages persistence as shared infra, delete the parallel propose/confirm brain, route everything through the (rewritten) controller. Fix out_full at :181 immediately if it survives another week.

verdicts.mechanism: dispatcher.py — the activation loop (task queue -> wake agents)
verdicts.why: Queue hygiene is genuinely production-grade: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claims (:54-66), lease heartbeat so long-running live workers aren't reaped (:78-108), linear backoff + dead-letter with paging (:117-139), circuit-breaker defer for paused apps (:161-181). But the throughput story is a toy: MAX_PER_TICK=2 (:33) — two tasks per scheduler tick, one process, one box. At 'hundreds of thousands of users each launching millions of dollars of business' this is a bicycle courier for a logistics empire. There is no worker pool, no horizontal scaling, no per-tenant fairness — a burst from one tenant starves the queue for everyone (compounded by factory's global 8-agent semaphore).
verdicts.action: Keep the claim/lease/dead-letter semantics; run N long-lived workers pulling continuously (the Postgres queue already supports it — project.py:45 even name-checks 'the cloud worker-pool path' that doesn't exist), with per-tenant concurrency quotas and priority aging.

verdicts.why: The 'ambient visibility into what the whole agent fleet is doing' is a pgrep-based ANSI terminal snapshot for the box owner (fleet.py:30-56): five hardcoded process patterns, emoji dots, last-14 audit rows, a while/sleep watch loop. Zero tenancy — it shows every tenant's activity to whoever runs the script. As an operator devtool it is fine; as the fleet-visibility story for a CEO who 'is briefed like a real CEO' it does not exist (the CEO-facing surfaces live elsewhere in console/cockpit, but nothing here shows an org chart, who is working on what, or per-company activity).
verdicts.action: Keep as an ops devtool but stop calling it fleet visibility; the real deliverable is a per-tenant, per-company live org view (agents as durable entities with current task/status) fed by the actor runtime — which requires the runtime to exist first.

missing: An agentic decision layer in the LIVE path: not one production decision — next phase, approval interpretation, escalation, notification, org expansion, hiring — is made by a model. Everything the CEO actually touches is regex + if/else (loopcontroller) or a fixed script (factory/project). The north star's core sentence is simply not implemented.

Company life after DELIVER: the org ships one product and the controller thread becomes a dumb Q&A bot forever (no phase reset, no second product, no v2, no ops). 'FAANG-grade internal processes — support, incident response, post-mortems, planning, review cycles — run autonomously' has no orchestration home at all; a company here is a one-shot build funnel.

Concurrent workstreams within one company: controller_state holds exactly one phase, one job, one product per org. A real company builds, markets, and operates simultaneously; this one can do exactly one thing at a time.

Cross-company orchestration for the multi-company CEO: nothing allocates capacity, priorities, or attention across a CEO's several orgs — companies just contend blindly for one global 8-slot semaphore (factory.py:94) and a 2-task tick (dispatcher.py:33).

Horizontal scale of any kind: every agent is a subprocess/daemon-thread in one Python process on one WSL box. No worker pool, no distributed execution, no per-tenant isolation of compute. The 'cloud worker-pool path' is a comment (project.py:45), not code.

Durable agents as entities: 'hiring' and 'org growth' can't be AI decisions because there is nothing to hire — agents are stateless subprocess invocations with no identity, memory, or tenure. The recursive org exists only as in-memory Python objects inside an unwired demo.

Long-term company memory for the controller: 12-turn chat window (loopcontroller.py:1176) plus a context_brief; no accumulated knowledge of decisions, preferences, or product history that a real chief-of-staff would carry.
Mid-build steering: a CEO who changes requirements during IMPLEMENT can only cancel (kill-switch) and restart; pending_intent queues text for the NEXT gate but nothing re-plans in-flight work.

The bridge from orchestra to product: no migration plan, no feature flag, no callsite. The blueprint's centerpiece (event-driven escalate/resolve/resume/broadcast) has been proven only against stubbed models in offline selftests — it has never made a single real decision.
churn_moments: The plan card appears; the CEO types 'hmm, this is not good — the pricing model is wrong' — _affirmative's \bgood\b regex (loopcontroller.py:1239) reads that as approval and launches the paid build with the wrong pricing model. Same for 'ready in what sense?' and 'don't do it yet' ('do it').

A perfectly healthy 35-minute build crosses RUNNING_TIMEOUT_MIN=30 (loopcontroller.py:993): the sweeper marks it crashed, the CEO gets '⚠️ The IMPLEMENT step hit a problem and stopped: worker timed out / crashed' while agents are still spending their money — and when the build finishes green, the guarded write (loopcontroller.py:365-370) throws the successful result away.

First product ships; the CEO says 'amazing — now build the companion mobile app.' Phase is parked at DELIVER forever, so the reply comes from the generic 'Answer the CEO briefly' fall-through (loopcontroller.py:721) and nothing is ever built again. The suggested next step is literally 'Start another org' (loopcontroller.py:984).

The CEO runs two companies and kicks off builds in both: both funnel into one global BoundedSemaphore(8) (factory.py:94) and a dispatcher that processes 2 tasks per tick (dispatcher.py:33). Company B's 'elite AI workforce' is a queue position.

An investor asks to see the 'elastic recursive org that grows itself': the only runnable demonstration is `orchestra.py demo`, whose every AI decision is a hardcoded JSON string in _make_demo_agent (orchestra.py:287-336) — a canned puppet show, discoverable in one glance at the source.

One component of a complex build hits a missing credential: project.py has no escalation path — the whole run ends BLOCKED_AT_COMPONENTS (project.py:392-394) and the multi-billion-dollar company asks its CEO to go fix it and type 'retry'.

The CEO asks the quick-build orchestrator for something ambitious; the model writes a long reply and orchestrator.py:181 parses the tail-truncated 'out' — the proposal silently loses its front, a bug the sibling controller fixed and documented months ago (loopcontroller.py:1203-1206) but that still lives in two other callers (orchestrator.py:181, orchestra/actor.py:240).
full.headline: We sold 'every decision is AI' and shipped a nine-phase regex waterfall that approves builds when the CEO says 'not good', kills healthy builds at minute 30, goes mute after shipping one product per company — while the actual AI org engine sits in a demo folder with zero production callers, running canned JSON puppet strings one agent at a time.

full.domain: Agent skill/quality — roles, role_brief, model/effort routing, agent tools, customagents, skills/extensions, memory/learning

verdicts.why: The prose is genuinely good (backend-engineer.yaml's verify-first responsibilities, visa-travel-advisor's cite-the-primary-source discipline), but this is a library of essays, not employees. (1) Only ~6 of 92 roles are ever dispatched by the pipeline (product-manager, builder, design-ux, reviewer, tech-lead + 'qa-security' which is just a trace label on a deterministic script — factory.py:1361-1596); grep across scripts/ shows ~60 roles referenced by exactly 1 file (the catalog itself). (2) Declared-not-wired, the repo's own known bug-class: `definition_of_done`, `flags_to`, and `ownership` are consumed by ZERO code — governance.py reads tools/paths/caps, role_brief() reads summary/responsibilities/must_never/communicates_via (factory.py:171-176) and silently drops the DoD and the entire escalation routing table the yamls so carefully specify. (3) The manifests are internally impossible: backend-engineer's DoD demands 'migrations run up and down on a real DB with output attached' while the factory never grants Bash (see tools verdict). (4) Sloppy caps a due-diligence buyer would flag: visa-travel-advisor.yaml has `can_read_secrets: true` and `can_modify_code: true` for an advisory role. (5) 71/92 share the identical copy-pasted must_never block; 33 share the identical tools line. (6) The tenant-facing org chart (orgview.py:35-46) lists 'planner', 'qa', 'security', 'devops' — roles that don't even have manifests — so the org the CEO sees and the org that governs don't agree.
verdicts.action: Fix: (a) wire definition_of_done into the agent prompt AND into a machine-checked hand-off gate (agent must attach evidence per DoD item; factory rejects hand-off without it); (b) wire flags_to into real routing — when an agent emits a flag, spawn/notify the named role; (c) reconcile orgview.ORG with the manifests; (d) audit caps (can_read_secrets) across all 92; (e) either dispatch the specialist roles from the pipeline (frontend work → frontend-engineer, migrations → database-admin) or delete them — a catalog of 86 never-hired employees is inventory fraud against the north star.

verdicts.why: One static f-string per role: a 'top hire at Jane Street, Google, or McKinsey' pep talk + responsibilities + must_never (factory.py:177-196). Motivational prose is not skill. It injects: no definition_of_done, no flags_to routing (the agent is told to 'raise it via org_channel' — a string, not a mechanism), no skills/playbooks, no examples of prior accepted work, no company/tenant context, no memory of previous builds, no output contract. Every spawn is a cold `claude -p` amnesiac that has never met the company it works for. The light/chat path (factory.py:509-514) drops even the role charter — reasonable for latency, but it means the CEO's live conversation is with a one-line persona on Haiku.
verdicts.action: Rebuild the brief as a layered context pack: (1) role charter incl. DoD as an explicit output contract; (2) the role's skill playbooks (progressive disclosure — see skills verdict); (3) tenant/company memory file (past decisions, product context, lessons); (4) concrete flags_to routing with the actual mechanism to invoke; (5) 1-2 exemplars of accepted work for the role. Cache the static prefix (prompt caching) so cost stays flat.

verdicts.why: Routing is a two-knob static env config: BUILD_MODEL=claude-opus-4-8 for heavy stages, CHEAP_MODEL=claude-haiku-4-5 for 'low-stakes' (factory.py:96-98). But look at what got labeled low-stakes: the REVIEWER whose REQUEST-CHANGES verdict is load-bearing for launch runs on Haiku (factory.py:1527), the design-quality craft gate runs on Haiku (1457), and the LAUNCH docs run on Haiku (1596). The cheapest model in the lineup is the ship/no-ship judge — a skeptical CEO paying for a 'FAANG-grade review cycle' is getting a $0.002 rubber stamp. There is no effort routing at all: the CLI's effort control is never touched, and extended thinking is actively DISABLED on the streaming path (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0, factory.py:835,842) including for non-chat stage work routed through _run_once_stream. The pre-flight 'estimate handshake' burns a full extra Haiku subprocess per spawn just to guess a timeout (factory.py:210-230) — the API's task-budget/effort primitives do this natively. Credit where due: model IDs and the _PRICES table (factory.py:716-717) are current and correct, fallback chains (opus→sonnet, claude→codex) are real, and per-tenant BYO-key isolation is properly threaded.
verdicts.action: Build a per-stage capability matrix: reviewer and security verification on BUILD_MODEL at high/xhigh effort (non-negotiable — the gate must be smarter than the builder, or at least as smart); builder at high effort with adaptive thinking ON for build stages (keep thinking off only for chat); chat/notifications on Haiku. Replace the estimate-handshake subprocess with effort + task-budget parameters. Make the matrix data (roles×stages→model,effort) a governed config, not env vars.

verdicts.mechanism: Tools available to agents (web, code exec, integrations)
verdicts.why: The factory grants agents exactly two tools: WebSearch and WebFetch (AGENT_TOOLS, factory.py:104), plus file edits via --permission-mode acceptEdits (factory.py:302-309). Bash — which every build prompt ('make `python -m pytest -q` pass', factory.py:1434-1436) and every engineering role's DoD depends on — is NEVER granted by the factory. The only reason agents can execute anything today is that the operator's personal ~/.claude/settings.json contains allow:[Bash,Edit,Write,...] with defaultMode bypassPermissions, which spawned `claude` subprocesses inherit. The platform's core capability rides on a dev dotfile: deploy this on any other machine and every builder goes limp mid-task while the prompts keep demanding test output. research_fleet.py:81 even admits the inversion in a comment ('it has Write even with tools=[]'). The role manifests' positive `tools:` list is consumed only to compute DENIALS (governance.spawn_restrictions) — never grants. Beyond that: zero MCP servers, zero SaaS integrations (no email, Slack, GitHub, CRM, ads platforms, analytics, payments), no browser automation for agents (playwright exists only in the QA harness), no document/spreadsheet tooling. The north star says 'all possible skills and extensions available'; the actual surface is 'can Google and can type'.
verdicts.action: Rewrite the grant layer: derive --allowedTools from the role manifest's tools list (explicit, versioned, per-role), sandbox Bash properly (the srt sandbox already exists for QA — extend it to agent Bash), and stop depending on user-level settings (spawn with an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / explicit settings file). Then build the integration tier: MCP servers per capability (GitHub, email/calendar, Slack, analytics, ads) wired to roles via the manifest, with governance deny-rules as the second layer. Without this, 80 of the 92 roles physically cannot do their stated jobs.

verdicts.why: The tenancy engineering is genuinely solid: ownership checks on every mutation, injection scan + untrusted-envelope on instructions, tenant-key routing, scheduler wiring, read-only system tier with sole-spawner invariant, and a selftest that actually proves the guards (customagents.py:90-357). But as a product capability it's a toy: a tenant 'hires' from a hardcoded allowlist of FOUR roles (ALLOWED_ROLES, line 51) out of the 92 advertised; the agent's entire output surface is a markdown file dropped into a repo plus a passive changelog notification (lines 153-171); there is no update/edit path for instructions (define/toggle/delete only), no conversation with the agent, no tool configuration, no memory across runs, no report quality gate — whatever the model wrote lands in the feed unreviewed, from a role whose charter promises 'traceable to a named authoritative source' with nobody checking.
verdicts.action: Fix: expand the allowlist to every advisory-safe governed role; add an edit path and a per-agent conversation thread; give recurring agents a memory file so week 5's market update knows what week 4 said; run outputs through the same review gate products get before they reach the CEO's feed; let the tenant attach integrations (their GA4, their repo) per agent.

verdicts.why: The docstring claims 'Roles query this so an agent KNOWS its capabilities' — no agent ever queries it. The catalog is a static Python list seeded into a DB whose only consumer is orchestrate.nearest_role() doing keyword substring matching to pick a role name (orchestrate.py:100-113). It is never injected into role_brief, never surfaced in any agent prompt, and most entries with engine 'claude' are literally the statement 'Claude does it natively' — i.e., the skill IS the absence of a skill. There are no actual skill packages: no per-role playbooks, no SKILL.md-style progressive-disclosure documents, no procedures an agent loads when the task calls for it. Against 'extremely skilled agents with ALL possible skills and extensions', this is an aspirational spreadsheet.
verdicts.action: Replace with a real skills system: per-capability playbook packages (procedure, checklists, examples, tool bindings) stored in control-plane, mapped to roles in the manifest, and loaded into the agent's context on demand (description in the brief, full playbook read when relevant — the pattern Claude Code skills already prove). The tool-engine rows (ffmpeg, playwright, blender) should become executable tool grants, not catalog rows.

verdicts.mechanism: Agent memory / learning from past work
verdicts.why: Elite employees compound; these agents are goldfish. The OS records plenty — full I/O traces (factory.py:43-59), build_outcomes via qualityloop.py, a recommender over them (recommend.py) — but not one byte of it ever re-enters an agent's context. recommend.py's output goes to the tenant UI ('add a security pass'), not to the agents who would act on it. There is no lessons store, no post-mortem-updates-the-charter loop, no per-tenant company memory, and the librarian role (librarian.yaml exists) is never invoked by anything. The improve.py/qualityloop.py loops iterate a PRODUCT toward a bar, but the ORG learns nothing: the builder that shipped the same manifest.json bug in March will ship it again in July, in front of a CEO who fired human employees for less. The north-star claim 'gets smarter as builds accumulate' (recommend.py docstring) is true only of a dashboard widget.
verdicts.action: Build the memory spine: (1) per-tenant company memory file(s) injected into every agent brief (decisions, product context, preferences); (2) per-role lessons store — post-mortem after every BLOCKED/fix-loop build distills a lesson, librarian-role agent curates it, role_brief loads the top-N for that role+kind; (3) feed recommend.py's strategy output into build_product's stage parameters, not just the UI. The traces DB you already have is the raw material — it's just write-only today.

verdicts.why: Right instinct ('only a claim until you have a number', eval_factory.py:1-11), wrong scale: the benchmark is ~6 trivial specs (tempconv, csvstats, a color picker, a notes app) exercising exactly one role-chain. There is zero evaluation of the other ~86 roles — the tax-advisor, visa-advisor, and compliance roles that make factual claims to a CEO have no groundedness/citation eval at all, despite charters demanding 'zero unsourced assertions'. pass@1 on a temperature converter tells an acquirer nothing about whether the org is elite.
verdicts.action: Grow the bench along the product surface: per-role eval suites (advisory roles: citation-groundedness checks against fetched sources; engineering roles: graduated difficulty incl. multi-file/service builds; review roles: seeded-bug catch rate). Gate role-manifest and prompt changes on eval regression, the way code is gated on tests.

missing: A designed capability-grant layer: agent tool permissions currently inherit from the developer's personal ~/.claude/settings.json (allow Bash/Edit/Write, defaultMode bypassPermissions) — the single most deployment-breaking accident in the domain; on any other host every engineering agent loses code execution

MCP/integration tier: no email, calendar, Slack, GitHub, CRM, payments, ads, or analytics access for any agent — the CMO/CFO/support roles have no hands; 'all possible skills and extensions' is currently WebSearch+WebFetch
Persistent memory: no per-tenant company memory, no per-role lessons store, no cross-run agent memory of any kind; traces and build_outcomes are collected but never re-enter any agent's context
Real skill packages: no playbooks/SKILL.md-style procedures per role; skills.py is an unconsumed catalog
Learning loop: no post-mortem→charter/prompt update cycle; the org never gets better at being an org, only individual products get improve.py'd

flags_to escalation routing: every role yaml specifies who to flag to; no mechanism exists to deliver a flag to that role — inter-agent 'communication' in the build line is two hardcoded delegate/done rows written by the factory for the dashboard (_log_comm), not agent-to-agent messages

Dynamic org growth: north star demands 'elastic recursive orgs that grow themselves'; can_spawn is false for every role except controller, can_request_hire is consumed at exactly one gate in orchestrate.py, and the 15 engineering specialists are never hired by the line — the org cannot actually expand to meet work
Effort/extended-thinking utilization: no effort parameter anywhere, thinking explicitly disabled (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0) on streamed runs — the platform pays for Opus and then lobotomizes it
definition_of_done enforcement: DoD exists in 92 manifests and is enforced nowhere — no evidence-attached hand-off gate
Per-role evals for the 86 non-engineering roles, especially factual-grounding checks for advisory roles that promise cited, dated, authoritative sources
full.headline: We're selling a 92-role elite workforce, but 86 of the badges are props, the six real workers can only run code because the founder's laptop settings accidentally allow it, the ship/no-ship reviewer is the cheapest model in the catalog, and not one agent remembers anything it learned yesterday.
churn_moments: The CEO deploys anywhere but the founder's WSL box and every 'engineer' silently loses Bash: builders write tests they can never run, claim done anyway, and the QA loop burns 3 fix attempts on failures the agent literally cannot reproduce — the CEO watches a $50 build flail on what looks like incompetence (factory.py:104 grants only WebSearch/WebFetch; capability comes from ~/.claude/settings.json)

The CEO opens the Agents view expecting to staff their company, sees a 92-role org, tries to hire — and gets a dropdown of 4 roles whose entire work-product is a markdown file and a passive notification (customagents.py:51,153-171). That's the moment 'indistinguishable from a real multi-billion-dollar company' dies

The CEO asks the visa/tax advisor a real question with money on the line; the charter promises named-source, date-checked citations, but no eval, no reviewer, and no verification ever checks a single claim before it lands in their feed — the first confidently wrong fee or deadline is the last question they ask

Week 4: the same builder ships the same category of bug it shipped in week 1, and the 'org' shows zero sign of having learned — a human employee would have been managed out; an AI employer that can't learn confirms every skeptic's prior

A board member's technical diligence reads factory.py and finds the launch-blocking code review runs on Haiku while the code was written by Opus (factory.py:1527 vs 96) — the review theater unravels the entire 'FAANG-grade process' pitch in one file

The CEO messages their 'Backend Engineer' expecting the accountable owner described in its charter and gets a cold-spawned amnesiac that has never seen their company, their prior builds, or its own definition of done

full.domain: FAANG internal-process coverage (alerts, incidents, digest, approvals, findings, help/support, forecast, experiments, improve, accountability, chaos, dogfood, intel + scheduler/watchdog/responder wiring)

verdicts.mechanism: alerts.py — agent-to-agent alerting with dedup + owner routing
verdicts.why: The code is competent (UNIQUE partial index dedup, route-on-new via orchestrate.request_collaborator) but it is DEAD CODE: grep across scripts/ shows zero importers and zero CLI callers — watchdog.py, responder.py, and the dashboard all page the owner's ntfy phone directly and never raise an owned alert. The docstring's 'escalatable' is fiction: there is no escalation sweep, no severity-based SLA, no re-route when an owner ignores an alert. This is the repo's own documented 'declared-not-wired' bug-class, again.
verdicts.action: Wire it: make watchdog.tick() and responder escalations raise alerts.raise_alert() instead of (not in addition to) raw ntfy, add an age-based escalation sweep (like findings.sweep) registered in scheduler.DEFAULT_SCHEDULES, and surface open alerts in the tenant console. Until something calls it, delete it from the capability story.
verdicts.files: /home/swami/projects/agent-os/scripts/alerts.py:2-17 (docstring promises), grep: no callers; /home/swami/projects/agent-os/scripts/watchdog.py:126-150 (pages ntfy directly, never raises an alert)

verdicts.why: It IS wired (watchdog.py:145 calls incident.investigate for novel crit issues), but the diagnosis context is a joke for the bar: last 12 lines of 5 HARDCODED dev log paths — including '/tmp/factory-splitbill2.log', a leftover from one specific dev build (incident.py:26) — plus 12 audit rows. The docstring claims 'the recommended action is only executed if it falls in the responder's safe allowlist' (incident.py:6-8); NOTHING parses or executes the '## Recommended next action' section — grep finds no consumer. RCAs are loose .md files in docs/incidents/ with no DB record, no severity, no timeline, no action items filed to findings.py, no tenant-facing comms, and no postmortem review loop.
verdicts.action: Store incidents in Postgres with severity/status/timeline; gather context dynamically (logs discovered from the process table, audit filtered to the affected resource, recent deploys); actually parse the recommended action and hand it to responder's allowlist or file it via findings.file() so it has an owner; auto-publish a tenant-facing incident + postmortem via notifications/statuspage.

verdicts.why: This would end a demo on the spot. daily() HARDCODES 'real paying users: 0 — no product is deployed/sold yet' (digest.py:88) and a canned market take about pomodoro apps — 'a tier-a commodity… per the intel report' (digest.py:93-94) — into EVERY tenant's brief forever, regardless of their actual business. recommendations() is a five-branch if/else template (digest.py:19-43), the opposite of the north star's 'every decision agentic'. It is owner-facing single-user (notify.send to one ntfy topic), not per-tenant. And despite the docstring 'Schedule it weekly', it is scheduled NOWHERE — not in scheduler.DEFAULT_SCHEDULES (scheduler.py:43-54), no cron, no boot script. The founder's standing brief never arrives.
verdicts.action: Rebuild as a per-tenant agentic chief-of-staff brief: an agent reads that tenant's real portfolio, builds, spend, open approvals, incidents, and findings, writes a prioritized brief with reasoning, delivered via notifications.send(tid,...) on a registered schedule. Zero hardcoded business commentary.

verdicts.why: The best-wired piece (console.py:386,452 exposes inbox+decide; a real selftest exercises all five kinds). But it has an acquisition-killing cross-tenant hole: _hire_requests() (approvals.py:97-102) and _dead_letters() (approvals.py:105-112) have NO tenant filter — every tenant sees every other tenant's hire requests and dead-task titles/errors (the selftest even admits 'global, surfaces in every tenant's inbox', line 262) — and decide() applies a hire_request approval with no ownership check (approvals.py:216-219), so paying tenant A can approve/deny tenant B's hires. blocked_build has an ownership check (line 222); the others don't. Also purely pull: nothing notifies the CEO that a decision is waiting.
verdicts.action: Tenant-scope hire_requests and dead_letters at the schema level (add tenant_id, filter in queries, enforce in decide() for every kind, not just blocked_build); fire notifications.send(tid, ...) when an item enters the inbox; add per-item context/recommendation so the CEO decides in one glance.

verdicts.why: Architecturally the right idea (file → route via orchestrate.request_collaborator → taskboard → resolve, no silent drops) and the routing/re-route logic is real. But the SLA guarantee is fake: findings.sweep — 'a finding cannot quietly rot' (findings.py:109) — is called by NOTHING; it's not in scheduler.DEFAULT_SCHEDULES and no cron exists, so an unresolved finding rots silently forever. No dedup either: the weekly dogfood pass will re-file the same 'password reset missing' finding every rotation, inflating the backlog. Escalation is a ntfy to the owner's phone, not a re-route to a different agent.
verdicts.action: Register 'findings-sweep' in DEFAULT_SCHEDULES (hourly); add a signature-based dedup like alerts.py's UNIQUE partial index; on SLA breach, escalate agentically (re-route to a senior role / raise priority) instead of only pinging the human.

verdicts.why: Wired to the console (console.py:403,440) and the GOTO validation is tidy, but as 'support' for a CEO product it's a static 13-entry FAQ (KNOWLEDGE dict, helpagent.py:31-104) with an LLM paraphraser. It's hand-maintained Python — guaranteed to drift from the real UI. It takes tid as a parameter and IGNORES it: it cannot answer 'why is MY build stuck', 'what did I spend yesterday', or anything about the user's actual state. No conversation memory, no ticket/escalation path when it can't help, no feedback loop into findings. A skeptical CEO asks one real question, gets a brochure answer, and files this under toy.
verdicts.action: Ground the assistant in live tenant state (portfolio, cockpit, approvals, forecast, recent incidents — the modules already exist) with tool access; auto-generate the screen map from the console nav definition; add 'escalate to support' that files a tracked ticket (findings.file) when confidence is low.

verdicts.why: The math, idempotent thresholds, re-arm, and send-before-mark failure handling are genuinely good, and it's per-tenant via notifications.send. But the whole point — pre-emptive alerts firing WITHOUT the user asking — never happens: the docstring claims 'A scheduler job runs check_alerts across tenants' (forecast.py:8), yet no scheduler job exists (scheduler.py:43-54) and nothing calls sweep(). Only the read-side forecast() is consumed (cockpit.py:257, console.py:389). The #1 CEO anxiety the file names ('am I about to blow my budget?') is answered only if the CEO happens to look. Also naive: straight-line 30-day projection with no burst handling.
verdicts.action: One line of real fix: register ('forecast-sweep', forecast.py sweep, 3600) in DEFAULT_SCHEDULES and add a selftest asserting it (the repo already has test_callsites_wired.py for exactly this bug-class). Then improve the projection with recent-window weighting.

verdicts.why: A 63-line checkbox. No _ensure()/CREATE TABLE anywhere in the repo — it assumes an 'experiments' table someone made by hand. Zero product callers: no build stage, no agent, no loop ever calls log_run/compare/best. And the CLI is broken in the dumbest possible way: line 63 reads `_demo() if (len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "demo") else _demo()` — EVERY invocation, args or not, inserts fake 'yt-clone' recommender rows into the production database. There is also no user-facing experimentation at all (A/B tests, rollouts) anywhere in scripts/, which is what a real company means by 'experiments'.
verdicts.action: Delete this file. Build experimentation that serves the product loop: (a) platform-level A/B + feature-flag rollout for tenant-facing changes (flags.py exists — connect it), with metrics.py as the outcomes ledger and automatic promote/rollback; (b) if agent-tuning experiments are wanted, integrate them into qualityloop/eval_factory where runs actually happen.
verdicts.files: /home/swami/projects/agent-os/scripts/experiments.py:23-29,63; grep: no CREATE TABLE experiments, no callers

verdicts.mechanism: improve.py — continuous improvement with safe-deploy gate
verdicts.why: Actually wired (qualityloop.py:163 calls improve_once inside the quality loop, which loopcontroller.py:952-953 drives), and promote-on-pass/revert-on-fail is a real gate. But 'safe deploy' is one agent run judged by one verify() pass — a flaky verifier either ships a regression or throws away good work, with no second opinion and no record of WHAT changed (audit payload is just {rigor, focus}, improve.py:58-59). Snapshot/rollback is shutil.copytree to /tmp instead of a git commit — no diff, no history, no review of the improvement. No lock: an improve round concurrent with a build or a second improve on the same repo silently corrupts the tree. Focus is a hardcoded string, not driven by production telemetry, user findings, or metrics.
verdicts.action: Make each round a git branch + commit with the diff attached to the audit/finding; gate on verify PLUS the product's own test suite and a reviewer-agent pass; take a per-product advisory lock shared with factory.py; pick focus from open findings/metrics instead of the hardcoded 'robustness, quality and performance'.

verdicts.why: The detection is real (request/resolve intent matching over conversations, grace window, per-agent reliability) and the selftest proves it. But the payoff is severed: sweep() — 'so the FLEET catches breakdowns itself' (accountability.py:9,109) — is scheduled NOWHERE and called by nothing; escalation is a ntfy ping to the one human phone, not a re-route of the dropped task to another agent; and reliability scores drive NOTHING — orchestrate.request_collaborator picks assignees purely by queue depth (orchestrate.py:185-193), so a 0.2-reliability agent keeps receiving work forever. That's a perf-review process that never affects staffing. Also full-table Python scan per call — fine today, dead at 100k tenants.
verdicts.action: Register the sweep in DEFAULT_SCHEDULES; on a dropped handoff, agentically re-route the original task (findings.file or orchestrate re-request to a different instance) instead of paging the human; feed reliability into request_collaborator's instance choice and into hire/retire decisions; push the matching into SQL.

verdicts.why: 65 lines, TWO scenarios (kill dashboard, kill api on hardcoded localhost ports), manual-only — never scheduled, not in any regression gate. The kill mechanism is pgrep -f pattern matching (chaos.py:29-30,45-49), which on any shared/multi-tenant host is a loaded gun. It never touches the failures that actually hurt: Postgres outage, provider 429/timeout storms, a factory build SIGKILLed mid-stage, disk-full during snapshot, a wedged dispatcher queue, ntfy down (silent paging failure). 'Proves the self-healing actually works' currently means 'proves two dev daemons restart'.
verdicts.action: Expand to a scenario matrix covering DB down, provider-error injection (fault flag in factory.agent), mid-build kill + resume-sweep recovery, disk pressure, and queue wedge, each with a recovery-time SLO; register a periodic game-day run in the scheduler and gate releases on the scorecard; target PIDs from the daemon registry, not pgrep patterns.

verdicts.mechanism: dogfood.py — standing acceptance pass (rotating demanding personas)
verdicts.why: The right instinct — 9 skeptic personas filing findings to owners, actually registered in the scheduler and selftested against that registration (dogfood.py:123-125). But the cadence destroys it: interval 604800s means ONE persona per WEEK (scheduler.py:53), so a full lap of the 9 personas takes NINE WEEKS — the north star says one frustration = churn, and 'feature-completeness' gets checked six times a year. Worse, the personas can't do their jobs: the agent is told to 'curl the HTML/JSON routes' (dogfood.py:84-85) — the accessibility, mobile-390px, keyboard-only, latency, and streaming personas are physically impossible over curl. No dedup, so each pass re-files the same findings into an already-unswept backlog.
verdicts.action: Run daily (all personas or a fast rotation); drive a real browser (the repo already has console_e2e.cjs / playwright-style harnesses) with screenshots for the UX/accessibility/latency personas; dedup findings by signature before filing.

verdicts.why: A one-shot 'run an agent, write MARKET.md' wrapper with no process around it: never scheduled, no freshness/refresh policy, no verification of the cited data, doesn't feed planning or the build loop — its only product-loop presence is the digest hardcoding a stale conclusion about one report ('per the intel report', digest.py:93-94) and telling the CEO to go run a CLI command (digest.py:42). The selftest is theater: it checks that a role YAML file exists at a hardcoded path in ~/projects/control-plane (intel.py:50-51) and asserts nothing about behavior.
verdicts.action: Make it a standing per-product process: scheduled refresh with staleness tracking, diffs against the previous report, and recommendations filed as findings/taskboard items so intel actually changes what gets built; replace the selftest with a mocked-agent behavioral test like helpagent's.

missing: Planning cycles: no planning process at all — no goal/OKR decomposition, no roadmap, no weekly/quarterly planning or prioritization ritual; taskboard.py is a flat list. 'Planning' is one of the north star's named processes and it simply does not exist.

Post-mortem process: incident.py writes an RCA .md and stops. No blameless review, no action items filed to owners (findings.py exists and is not called), no 'did we fix the class of bug' follow-up, no incident database or trend analysis.

Performance management / hiring consequences: accountability.reliability() computes scores nobody consumes; there is no eval of a newly hired agent, no derating, retraining, or retiring of unreliable agents, no promotion of strong ones. Hiring is a status flip on hire_requests.
Real customer support: no ticketing system, no support SLA, no human-escalation path, no per-tenant support history. helpagent is a static FAQ; a CEO with a real problem has nowhere to go.

Security as a process: security_scan.py is a regex self-scan of the platform tree, invoked only via risk.py on demand — no schedule, no dependency/CVE scanning of the products the factory ships to customers, no secrets rotation, no pen-test cadence.

Tenant-facing incident communication: watchdog/responder/incident all page ONE owner ntfy topic; statuspage.py binds 127.0.0.1; affected tenants are never told their build/provider is degraded, and no postmortem is ever published to them.

On-call/escalation policy: a single human phone is the pager for every tenant and every severity — at 'hundreds of thousands of users' this is one person drinking from a firehose; no rotation, no severity-based routing, no agentic first-responder tiers for product issues.
Retro cadence: metrics.py promises KPIs 'surfaced in the daily digest / monthly retro' — no retro job, command, or document generator exists anywhere.
User-facing experimentation: no A/B testing, no staged rollouts, no cohort analysis for the products tenants launch — 'experiments.py' is an ML-run logger with no callers.
Comms/PR and legal/compliance review processes: nothing (launch_kit generates marketing assets, but there is no review/comms process).
churn_moments: The CEO's 'daily digest' tells every tenant, every day, 'real paying users: 0 — no product is deployed/sold yet' plus a hardcoded hot-take about pomodoro apps, regardless of their actual business (digest.py:88,93-94) — instant credibility death.
Tenant A opens Approvals and sees tenant B's hire requests and dead-task error messages — and can approve tenant B's hires (approvals.py:97-112,216-219). One screenshot of that kills the acquisition.

A CEO blows 100% of their token budget with zero warning because forecast's alert sweep — the file's entire reason to exist — was never scheduled; the wall the docstring promised to prevent is exactly what they hit.

A blocker-severity dogfood finding ('password reset is a stub') sits open for months: findings.sweep is unscheduled, so the 'no finding can rot' SLA never runs, and the 9-week persona rotation won't even re-check for two months.
CEO asks the help assistant 'why is my build stuck?' and gets a generic 'Open Cockpit to watch workers' brochure line, because the support agent ignores tenant state entirely.
An incident RCA cites /tmp/factory-splitbill2.log — a hardcoded artifact of the developer's own test build — as diagnostic context in a paying customer's incident.
full.headline: You've written the docstrings of a FAANG company and the wiring of a weekend project — half these 'processes' (alerts, forecast sweeps, findings SLAs, accountability, the digest itself) are never invoked by anything, and the one screen that is wired leaks other tenants' data.

full.domain: Human-pattern communication: commfabric.py, notifications.py, askuser.py, alerts.py, digest.py, loopcontroller._ping/_report/say, and the Assistant chat voice

verdicts.why: This is not a fabric; it is a proof-of-concept selftest wearing the fabric's name. The docstring says 'Proof choreography', the question is hardcoded ('is SendGrid v2 still supported?', line 77), the reply is hardcoded (line 89), the workflow id is handed between processes via /tmp/commfabric_wf_id (line 25), and the awaited party is the literal string 'responder'. Zero production callers: grep shows it referenced only in comments (orchestrate.py:15, bus.py:40) and a skills-catalog string. Worse, the typed message envelope it was supposed to carry — messaging.py with its FIPA intents including ESCALATE, PROPOSE, CLARIFY — has ZERO importers anywhere in the repo. The entire 'agents communicate like an elite org' vocabulary is declared, never wired (the owner's known declared-not-wired bug-class, again).
verdicts.action: Build the real thing the demo proves is possible: a production ask/await service where any agent (and the CEO surface) sends a typed messaging.Message over DBOS send/recv, with reply_by enforced, escalation on breach wired to accountability.overdue_waits(), and the wait-graph feeding deadlock detection. Delete the /tmp choreography or move it to tests/. Until orchestrate/fleet/loopcontroller actually import messaging.Message, the ADR-0005 layer is fiction.

verdicts.why: The feed/badge/prefs mechanics are sound, but two of its three channels are theater. Email: _email() imports 'emailer' (line 64) — emailer.py does not exist anywhere in the repo — so every 'email' delivery is a print() to stdout, forever, while send() happily reports the channel worked or silently degrades. Urgent: every tenant's urgent notification pages THE FOUNDER's personal ntfy phone (line 87, notify.send) — at the north-star's 100,000 users, the escalation architecture is one developer's phone; and push.py falls back to paging the founder too when a tenant has no topic. Finally, the level is chosen by hardcoded call sites, not intelligence: loopcontroller._ping defaults level='urgent' (loopcontroller.py:226) and every single ping in the file passes urgent — when everything is urgent, the taxonomy communicates nothing.
verdicts.action: Ship a real email transport (SMTP/provider) or delete the email column; sever the tenant-urgent→founder-pager coupling (founder gets platform incidents only); and move level selection out of call sites into an attention-manager decision (the north star explicitly says 'every notification decision is an intelligent AI decision, not hardcoded flow'). Add quiet hours, batching, and per-org channel routing.

verdicts.why: Dead code duplicating two other mechanisms. Its only repo consumer is selftest.sh. It polls a table (is_answered, line 75) — the exact anti-pattern commfabric's durable recv exists to kill — and its 'surface to the user' step is a try/except-pass import of agent_request (lines 52-57) that swallows every failure, so a question like 'approve this charge' or 'paste the 2FA code' can be filed into a table no UI reads and no one is ever told about. No deadline, no reminder, no escalation if the CEO doesn't answer, no priority, no notification fired. A real org that needs a decision from the CEO follows up; this files a row and hopes.
verdicts.action: Delete it. Fold the ask-the-human primitive into ONE mechanism: agent_request (which the console actually surfaces) backed by commfabric's durable suspend, with a mandatory reply_by, a notifications.send at standard/urgent based on what's blocked, automatic reminder escalation as the deadline approaches, and 'N decisions waiting on you' aggregated into the CEO's brief.

verdicts.mechanism: alerts.py — agent-to-agent alerting with dedup and ownership
verdicts.why: The route-to-owner + open-signature dedup design is genuinely right, but three gaps make it a toy at scale. (1) The dedup key is sha256 of the first 80 chars of free text (line 48): 'disk 91% full on node-7' vs 'disk 92% full on node-7' are different signatures, so the flapping-storm problem it exists to solve returns the moment a metric value is in the message. (2) severity is stored and never used — a 'critical' and a 'warn' get identical treatment: no faster routing, no founder page, no CEO surface, ever; open_alerts() ages in minutes but nothing consumes the age (no escalate-on-unowned, no re-route when the owner sits on it). (3) One consumer in the whole repo (osq.py) — the 'monitoring agent watching the fleet' in the docstring doesn't exist.
verdicts.action: Make signature a caller-supplied structured key (source+condition+resource, never message text); wire an aging sweep into scheduler.py that escalates unacknowledged criticals up the chain (owner → controller → CEO notification); actually emit alerts from monitor.py/appguard/incident so the mechanism has producers.

verdicts.why: This is the single most important artifact for the 'proactive briefing' bar and it fails on every axis. (1) It is never sent: DEFAULT_SCHEDULES in scheduler.py has no digest job — the 'schedule it weekly' in the docstring is an instruction to a human that nobody executed. (2) It goes to the wrong person: delivery is notify.send → the FOUNDER's ntfy topic; a paying tenant-CEO has no briefing surface at all. (3) It lies: daily() hardcodes the literal strings 'real paying users: 0 — no product is deployed/sold yet' (line 87) and a canned lecture that pomodoro is 'a tier-a commodity' (lines 93-94) — every user, every business, every day, forever, would read the same dev-notes-as-prose. (4) It's truncated to 1500 chars for ntfy (line 124). A skeptical CEO reading 'your company: pomodoro is a commodity' about their fintech startup churns instantly.
verdicts.action: Build the chief-of-staff brief: per-tenant, per-org, LLM-composed from real state (portfolio, open decisions, alerts, spend, in-flight jobs, overdue waits), delivered on a cadence the CEO sets, into the in-app feed + email, with a 'decisions waiting on you' section that deep-links to the gates. Zero hardcoded prose. Schedule it in DEFAULT_SCHEDULES per tenant.

verdicts.why: This is the best-engineered piece of the domain — honest ETA ranges, SLA re-warn, mid-flight intent queueing, duplicate suppression, status honesty during fleet runs are all real and CEO-grade in intent. But it contains the domain's worst churn bomb: _affirmative (line 1239) matches bare '\bgood\b', '\bready\b', '\bdo it\b', '\bperfect\b' — I verified: 'this does not look good', "don't do it", 'I am not ready yet', and 'this is far from perfect' ALL parse as approval and advance() — a CEO's explicit REJECTION locks the plan and fires a paid build. Second: at the generic user_feedback gate (line 706-712) a substantive change request ('make the team page read-only') gets the fixed string 'Got it — I'll fold that in.' — but nothing re-plans; IMPLEMENT dispatches from the stored plan JSONB (line 933-939), so the feedback is acknowledged and then silently discarded. Third: every _ping is urgent (line 226 default), flattening the taxonomy.
verdicts.action: Replace the affirmative/intent regexes with a cheap LLM intent classifier (approve / reject / revise / question / status) — the module already has a fast-model path (_llm light=True); on 'revise' at any gate, actually mutate the plan and confirm the diff back. Vary ping levels by event weight (ship=urgent, options-ready=standard).

verdicts.mechanism: Assistant chat voice — the persona the CEO talks to
verdicts.why: There is no assistant. console.py:113 admits it: 'module (assistant.py); until it does…' — assistant.py does not exist; org=0 falls back to the first company's build thread. The 'voice' is a scatter of per-phase hardcoded strings ('I'm your controller. Tell me what you want to build', line 386) and per-branch system prompts ('You are a product controller scoping a build for a non-technical CEO', line 625), with the catch-all being literally 'Answer the CEO briefly.' (line 721). No persistent persona, no name, no memory of the CEO across sessions or companies, no proactivity (it only ever speaks when spoken to or when a job lands), no disagreement ('Got it — I'll fold that in' is the only response to pushback), no negotiation, no 'your VP of Eng needs a decision' — no executive exists to need one. helpagent is a separate keyword-grounded FAQ bot. The north-star interaction — being briefed and consulted by an elite org — is architecturally absent: today it is exactly what the prompt feared, API events + toasts with a build-wizard bolted on.
verdicts.action: Build the chief-of-staff agent as a first-class module: one persistent account-level persona with memory (CEO preferences, standing decisions, risk tolerance), a proactive turn loop (it initiates: morning brief, decision chase-ups, anomaly flags), an executive cast (comms attributed to named role-agents: 'Priya, your Head of Research, recommends option 2 — I disagree, here's why'), and a policy of principled pushback sourced from real data. Route ALL user-facing copy through it so fixed strings die.

missing: A chief-of-staff layer, entirely: no per-tenant scheduled briefing, no 'decisions waiting on you' aggregation across companies, no follow-up when the CEO ignores a decision request. The only scheduled comms job in DEFAULT_SCHEDULES (scheduler.py:43-54) is the SLA watchdog.

Named executive personas and attribution: every message comes from 'the controller'; nothing can say 'your VP of Eng needs a decision' because no role-agent ever addresses the CEO — orchestrate/fleet agents are invisible to the human.
