Disagreement and negotiation: no code path anywhere pushes back on a CEO instruction with evidence, proposes an alternative, or negotiates scope/budget/timeline — the vocabulary for it (messaging.Intent.PROPOSE/ESCALATE/REJECT) exists with zero importers.

Intelligent attention management: the north star says every notification/escalation decision is an AI decision; today level/priority/channel are hardcoded at every call site and effectively always 'urgent'. No quiet hours, no batching, no interruption budget, no learning what this CEO wants to hear about.

Real delivery channels for tenants: no email transport exists (emailer.py is imported but absent), push requires a self-registered self-hosted ntfy topic, and both silently fall back — a CEO who closes the tab is reachable only by luck.
Cross-company CEO view: notifications, alerts, digests and asks are all per-tenant/org threads; nothing composes the multi-company picture the north star is named after.

Escalation etiquette upward from the fleet: agent_alerts and accountability dropped-ball detection never reach the tenant CEO — accountability.sweep() pages the platform founder (accountability.py:116-119) and isn't even scheduled.
Cadence rituals: no weekly business review, no post-ship retro to the CEO, no board-pack; the closest thing (digest.daily) is unscheduled, founder-only, and partially hardcoded fiction.
Acknowledgment tracking: nothing knows whether the CEO saw a decision request; no read-receipt-driven re-escalation anywhere.
churn_moments: The CEO reviews the plan and types 'this does not look good' — _affirmative (loopcontroller.py:1239) matches '\bgood\b', the gate clears, and a paid build fires against the rejected plan. Same for "don't do it", 'I am not ready yet', 'far from perfect' (verified by running the regex).

At the prototype gate the CEO says 'change the pricing page to annual billing' — gets 'Got it — I'll fold that in.' (loopcontroller.py:711), then says 'approve', and IMPLEMENT builds the original stored plan verbatim; the instruction was acknowledged and discarded.

The CEO's 'daily brief' — if anyone ever scheduled it — opens with 'real paying users: 0 — no product is deployed/sold yet' and a canned riff on pomodoro apps (digest.py:87-94) regardless of what their business is; and it arrives on the developer's phone, not theirs.

Every event lands as URGENT (loopcontroller._ping defaults, line 226) — options ready, prototype ready, overrun warning, ship — so within a day the bell means nothing and the one real emergency drowns.

An agent needs the CEO to 'approve this charge' via askuser.ask(); the surfacing hook is a swallowed try/except (askuser.py:52-57), no notification fires, no deadline exists — the loop waits forever and the CEO never knows they were asked.
A security-critical urgent for tenant #83,000 pages the founder's personal ntfy phone (notifications.py:87) while the tenant themself gets a print() to stdout because emailer.py doesn't exist.
full.headline: You promised me an executive team that briefs its CEO, and you shipped a build wizard that reads 'this does not look good' as approval, files my decisions into a table nobody watches, and sends my daily brief — hardcoded to say I have zero customers — to the developer's own phone.

This is a single-laptop appliance wearing a SaaS costume: one Python http.server behind a Tailscale tunnel, no payment processor, no connection pool, no rate limiting, app-level-only tenant isolation, and a single global advisory lock that serializes every audited action across all tenants on earth — it dies at ~50 concurrent users and cannot bill a dollar.

verdicts.why: The entire CEO-facing app is one Python process using stdlib http.server ThreadingHTTPServer, GIL-bound, one OS thread per connection, bound to 127.0.0.1 and exposed only via `tailscale serve` from a single WSL box (recover.sh:30). There is no reverse proxy, no worker pool, no process manager, no horizontal instances, no load balancer, no keep-alive (SSE sends Connection: close). A single SSE chat stream (console.py:1411-1471) blocks a whole thread for the entire model turn. At ~100 concurrent CEOs this is 100 GIL-contending threads on one box; at 10k it is a joke. A board member asked to 'run several multi-billion-dollar companies' is running them on your laptop over a VPN tunnel.
verdicts.action: Replace with a real ASGI app (FastAPI/uvicorn+gunicorn or equivalent) behind nginx/Envoy, stateless app instances behind a load balancer, TLS terminated at the edge, autoscaling on a container platform (k8s/ECS). The HTTP layer must be horizontally scalable and hold zero in-process state.

verdicts.mechanism: Database access: fresh psycopg.connect() per operation, no pooling
verdicts.files: 426 call sites across scripts/*.py; cockpit.py (8), loopcontroller.py (33); postgres/docker-compose.yml:12 (127.0.0.1:5433, single container, local volume)
verdicts.why: Every handler opens brand-new Postgres connections (TCP+auth+TLS handshake) per call — and a single cockpit render opens many (cockpit.py:113 plus nested), loopcontroller opens 33 distinct connect sites. Postgres default max_connections≈100. Even 30-50 concurrent users triggering cockpit exhausts connections and everything 500s. There is no pgbouncer/pool, no read replica, no HA, no off-box backup (just local .aosnap snapshots), single docker container on a local volume. This is a laptop database pretending to be a fleet backend.
verdicts.action: Introduce a real connection pool (pgbouncer + app-side pool), move to a managed/replicated Postgres (primary + read replicas), route read-heavy views to replicas, and cap per-request connection count to 1. Add HA + PITR backups off-box.

verdicts.mechanism: Global hash-chained audit log with a single advisory lock
verdicts.files: scripts/audit.py:60-75 (pg_advisory_xact_lock(742042) + SELECT entry_hash ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1); called from factory AgentRun, billing, auth, watchdog everywhere
verdicts.why: audit.append() takes ONE global advisory lock (742042) and reads the latest row to chain prev_hash before every insert. Every AgentRun, login, billing op, and governance decision platform-wide funnels through this single serialized mutex on one shared table. Two tenants on opposite sides of the planet block each other on every logged action. This is a hard, tenant-agnostic throughput ceiling that also makes audit_log an unbounded, unpartitioned, ever-growing single table (billions of rows) with only a ts index. It will be the first thing to melt under load.
verdicts.action: Make the audit chain PER-TENANT (or per-shard) so locks don't cross tenants, or switch to an append-only design that batches/streams to an external immutable store (e.g. per-tenant Merkle segments). Partition audit_log by tenant+time; never take a global lock on a hot write path.

verdicts.mechanism: Auth: bearer token = plaintext DB lookup, no cache, no rate limiting, no lockout
verdicts.files: scripts/tenancy.py:31-35 (SELECT tenant_id WHERE api_token=%s), scripts/auth.py (no throttle), scripts/console.py:1494 (_tenant per request)
verdicts.why: The API token is stored in cleartext in tenants.api_token — a single DB dump compromises every tenant. Every authenticated request does a synchronous DB round-trip to resolve token->tenant (no cache/JWT), adding load and latency to 100% of traffic. Login/signup/verify/reset endpoints (console.py:1509) have ZERO rate limiting, no failed-attempt lockout, no captcha: password brute-force is wide open, and the 6-digit email code (auth.py:86, 1M space, 15-min window) is brute-forceable with unlimited attempts (verify_email has no attempt counter).
verdicts.action: Hash tokens at rest (store only a hash, compare by hash); issue signed stateless sessions (JWT) to avoid per-request DB lookups; add per-IP/per-account rate limiting + exponential lockout on login/verify/reset; cap email-code attempts (e.g. 5) and rotate on failure.

verdicts.mechanism: Tenant isolation: application-level WHERE clauses only, no Postgres RLS
verdicts.files: scripts/tenancy.py:1-5 (docstring: 'at cloud scale, add row-level security'), postgres/initdb/12-tenancy.sql (no RLS), console.py:79-96 (_owns manual IDOR guard on a hardcoded route set)
verdicts.why: Isolation depends entirely on every query remembering to append `WHERE tenant_id=%s` / `product = ANY(prods)`. There is no Postgres row-level security — the schema comment literally defers it. One forgotten filter in any of 150 modules = silent cross-tenant data leak (a CEO seeing a competitor's fleet). The IDOR guard (_owns) is a hardcoded allow-list (ORG_SCOPED_GET/POST, console.py:92-96); any current or future route with a client-supplied id NOT in that set is unguarded, and _owns itself costs an extra query per request.
verdicts.action: Enable Postgres RLS with a per-connection tenant GUC (set_config('app.tenant_id', ...)) so the database enforces isolation regardless of app bugs; make tenant scoping structural, not per-query discipline. Add automated tests that fail if any query touches a tenant table without the RLS/tenant predicate.

verdicts.mechanism: Billing: no payment processor; in-app plan change is free
verdicts.files: scripts/billing.py:32-36 (PLANS dict), scripts/billingview.py:57-69 (change_plan just UPDATEs plan column, docstring admits 'money-free, Stripe OUT OF SCOPE')
verdicts.why: The product is pitched as 'sellable for hundreds of millions' but cannot collect a single dollar: there is no Stripe/card capture, no checkout, no dunning, no invoicing delivery. change_plan lets any tenant set themselves to 'enterprise' for free by hitting POST /api/billing/plan. Metering exists (settle/invoice) but nothing charges the card. This is a billing simulation, not a business.
verdicts.action: Integrate a real payment provider (Stripe): card capture at signup/upgrade, subscription + usage-based metering pushed to Stripe, webhook-driven plan state (never client-driven), failed-payment dunning + suspension. change_plan must require a completed payment intent, not a column flip.

verdicts.mechanism: Build/job execution: in-process daemon threads, not a durable queue
verdicts.files: scripts/console.py:367 (threading.Thread(frontdoor._run_build, daemon=True)), scripts/frontdoor.py:310, scripts/loopcontroller.py:251/374 (_work daemon threads)
verdicts.why: Builds and controller jobs run as daemon threads INSIDE the web process. If console.py restarts — watchdog relaunch (watchdog.py:39), deploy, OOM, crash — every in-flight build/job dies silently mid-run, orphaning the CEO's 'building…' spinner. A durable SKIP-LOCKED queue exists for dispatcher tasks (dispatcher.py:59) but frontdoor builds and loopcontroller jobs BYPASS it and live in-memory. There is no separation between the web tier and the compute tier, so scaling either means scaling both, and a busy build starves HTTP threads.
verdicts.action: Move all builds/controller jobs onto the durable Postgres SKIP-LOCKED queue (or a real broker), executed by a SEPARATE, horizontally-scalable worker fleet. The web tier only enqueues; workers claim, checkpoint, and are crash-recoverable. Nothing long-running runs in the request process.

verdicts.mechanism: Compute scaling + supervision: ~30-agent single-box ceiling, pgrep-based watchdog
verdicts.files: scripts/scale.py:11/20 (SINGLE_BOX_AGENT_CEIL=30, 'cloud-pool' is a label with no impl), factory.py:94 (AOS_MAX_AGENTS default 8 semaphore, ~430MB per claude subprocess), watchdog.py:37-39/85-87 (pgrep -fc on local box), responder.py:43-65 (local bash relaunch)
verdicts.why: scale.py openly admits the whole platform shares a ~30-concurrent-agent ceiling on one box (default semaphore of 8), and 'cloud-pool mode' is a returned string with no worker pool behind it. So ALL tenants combined share 8 heavyweight claude subprocesses; 100 CEOs each wanting a build means multi-hour queues. Supervision is single-box: watchdog counts local processes with pgrep and responder relaunches via local bash — there is no orchestrator, no health-based routing, no multi-instance failover. If the one box dies, the platform dies, and the watchdog dies with it.
verdicts.action: Implement the actual distributed worker pool the docstring promises (autoscaling worker nodes pulling the SKIP-LOCKED queue), with per-tenant fairness/quotas on compute. Replace pgrep supervision with a real orchestrator (k8s liveness/readiness probes, replicas, PodDisruptionBudgets) and off-box health checks.

missing: Payment processing entirely (no Stripe/card capture/dunning) — cannot collect revenue despite the 'hundreds of millions' bar
Connection pooling / pgbouncer — every request cold-opens Postgres connections; connection exhaustion at ~50 concurrent users
Postgres row-level security — isolation is app-level WHERE clauses only; one missed filter leaks cross-tenant data
Rate limiting / brute-force protection / account lockout on login, signup, email-code verification, and password reset

Horizontal scalability — single http.server process, single box, single Postgres container, exposed via one Tailscale tunnel; no load balancer, no app replicas, no read replicas, no DB HA/replication/off-box backups
Durable build/job queue for the front-door build path and loopcontroller jobs — they run as in-process daemon threads that vanish on restart
Token hashing at rest — api_token stored cleartext; a DB dump compromises every tenant
A real distributed worker pool — 'cloud-pool mode' is a label; actual concurrency is capped to ~8-30 agents on one box shared across ALL tenants
Platform-level observability/APM and per-tenant compute quotas (only build-count/token quotas exist, no CPU/RAM/agent fairness across tenants)
Audit-log partitioning + per-tenant chains — the global advisory lock + single unbounded table is a hard cross-tenant throughput ceiling and an ever-growing hot table
churn_moments: A skeptical CEO opens devtools and sees the app is served from 127.0.0.1 over a personal Tailscale tunnel — 'this is running on someone's laptop' — instant credibility collapse
Second concurrent demo user logs in and the whole console starts throwing 500/503s as Postgres connections exhaust
Trying to actually pay: clicks Upgrade, plan silently flips to Enterprise with no card ever charged — a serious buyer realizes there is no billing and walks
A build is mid-flight when the box hiccups/redeploys; the 'building…' bubble spins forever and the work is silently lost
An attacker (or a nervous security reviewer) points a login brute-forcer at the API and nothing stops them — no rate limit, no lockout

full.domain: trust for skeptics — spend controls, approvals, audit visibility, explainability, blast-radius containment
full.headline: "We have beautifully-engineered locks on the doors — but the two that matter most, the money circuit-breaker and the human-approval gate, are wired to nothing and never actually fire in production."

verdicts.why: The chain's integrity rests on a SINGLE symmetric secret (AUDIT_HMAC_KEY) sitting in .env.local on the same box as the Postgres it protects (audit.py:40-43). It is tamper-evident ONLY against an actor who lacks the key — but every agent process, the enforce_manifest hook (it shells the venv python that reads .env.local), and anyone with host access CAN read it, so an insider/compromised-agent can forge or rewrite the entire history undetectably. There is no external anchor (no notary, no WORM, no periodic hash publication, no asymmetric signature), so 'even an actor with Postgres write access' — the threat the docstring claims to defend — is NOT actually defended if they also have the box. verify() is real and well-built, and reseal()'s fail-closed self-consistency (audit.py:82-144) is genuinely good, but verify() only runs inside selftest.sh — it is on NO schedule, so tampering is never detected between manual runs.
verdicts.action: Move to per-tenant asymmetric signing (Ed25519, private key in an HSM/KMS the app server cannot exfiltrate) OR anchor the chain externally: append each block hash to an append-only external store (S3 Object-Lock WORM / a transparency log) on a schedule, and register `audit.py verify` as a DEFAULT_SCHEDULE job (every 5-10 min) that pages on BROKEN. Publish the head hash to the CEO daily so integrity is provable to a skeptic, not asserted.

verdicts.mechanism: governance.require_approval — hash-pinned, single-use, fail-closed human-approval gate
verdicts.why: This is the single most important trust control for 'the AI is about to spend real money / touch prod' — and it is DECLARED-NOT-WIRED. governance.require_approval() (governance.py:165-220) is a genuinely excellent gate (hash-pins the exact payload, expires, consumes single-use, fails closed on any error). But a repo-wide grep finds ZERO callers outside its own selftest. No deploy site, no spend site, no secret-read site calls it. factory.py calls governance.enforce(spawner_role,'spawn') for spawn (factory.py:427) but NOTHING calls require_approval before any high-blast-radius action. approval_required_for(controller) lists 'deploy' — a paper list that gates nothing. A skeptical CEO told 'deploys need your approval' would discover the approval is never actually demanded.
verdicts.action: Wire require_approval() at EVERY high-blast-radius action site: production deploy, raising a spend cap, vault PROD-secret read, cross-tenant action, org expansion. It must be the mandatory choke-point, with the approval_id flowing from the console/phone decision. Add a wiring guard test (like test_governance_wired.py) that FAILS if any capability in approval_required_for has no call site invoking require_approval.
verdicts.files: scripts/governance.py:143-220; scripts/factory.py:427 (enforce wired, require_approval NOT); grep: zero external callers of require_approval

verdicts.why: Elegant durable-workflow design (suspends at zero token cost, survives crash, phone reply → DBOS.recv), but it is a DEMO, not a system: it has zero importers/callers anywhere in the codebase, `resolve` explicitly 'stands in for' the real phone bridge (approval_gate.py:6-8), and it duplicates yet a THIRD parallel approval mechanism (alongside governance.require_approval and verify_approval.py) with none of them agreeing on which is canonical. Three half-wired approval systems is worse than one wired one — nobody can answer 'how does an approval actually work here'.
verdicts.action: Pick ONE approval spine. Make approval_gate.py's durable workflow the runtime gate, have it verify via verify_approval.py's hash-pin, and have governance.require_approval delegate to it. Wire the real reply_listener path (not the `resolve` stand-in) end to end and delete the other two implementations.
verdicts.files: scripts/approval_gate.py (no callers); scripts/governance.py:165; control-plane/scripts/verify_approval.py — three disjoint approval systems

verdicts.mechanism: appguard.py — per-app financial circuit-breaker (spend cap + loss-limit auto-pause)
verdicts.why: Two fatal wiring/economics bugs. (1) The sweep that ACTUALLY auto-pauses bleeders — appguard.guard()/evaluate() — is scheduled NOWHERE: it is absent from scheduler.DEFAULT_SCHEDULES, ticker.sh, and any cron; only selftest calls it. The dispatcher reads paused_apps() STATE (dispatcher.py:154) but nothing SETS that state on a cadence, so in the live loop the circuit-breaker never trips unless a human manually runs `appguard.py guard`. The docstring says 'run on a schedule' — that schedule does not exist. (2) revenue is HARDCODED 0.0 (appguard.py:72), so profit = -spend for every app; any real earning product that spends past its $20 default loss_limit would be auto-paused-as-a-bleeder the moment the sweep did run — a self-inflicted outage on your best products. RATE_PER_1K is also a fixed 0.003 proxy, not real model pricing.
verdicts.action: Register `appguard.py guard` as a DEFAULT_SCHEDULE job at a tight cadence (60-120s). Replace revenue=0.0 with real billing attribution before loss-limit logic can mean anything, or disable the loss_limit branch until revenue is wired (keep only the hard spend cap). Derive $/token from live model pricing, not a constant.
verdicts.files: scripts/appguard.py:72,95-107,123-126; scripts/scheduler.py:43-53 (no appguard job); scripts/dispatcher.py:148-156 (reads state nobody writes)

verdicts.why: It caps TOKENS, not dollars, and the call site fails OPEN: factory.py:497-501/688-693 wraps allow_spend in try/except with allowed=True on ANY error, so a transient budgets-DB hiccup silently removes the cap (comment even admits 'we fail OPEN'). est_tokens is a crude len(text)//4 + 8000 heuristic (factory.py:495) — an agent that reads large files or loops mid-run blows past the estimate with no mid-flight check. The CEO never sees a real-dollar number or a forecast at the moment of decision; a token integer is not a trust signal a skeptic accepts for 'millions of dollars of business'.
verdicts.action: Cap in DOLLARS with live pricing; enforce a per-run AND per-window (hourly/daily) dollar ceiling that re-checks mid-run, not just once pre-dispatch. On governor-infra error, fail CLOSED for high-cost dispatches (the soft USD cap is not a substitute). Surface remaining budget in dollars + burn-rate forecast in the console before every consequential action.

verdicts.mechanism: manifest_policy.py — canonical role/path/tool permission decision (blast-radius containment)
verdicts.why: This is the strongest thing in the domain. One source of truth consumed by BOTH the spawn-time --disallowedTools layer (governance.spawn_restrictions) and the deterministic PreToolUse hook (enforce_manifest.evaluate), so the two layers cannot diverge by construction. Hard-deny ALWAYS wins and is case-insensitive (closes the APFS/HFS '.ENV' bypass), '..' parent-traversal is denied for every role, the '**' write scope correctly refuses the control-plane governance surface (blocks manifest self-escalation and hook self-disable), Bash write-target extraction routes shell write vectors through the SAME is_denied_path predicate, and both selftests are thorough. This is real, defensible containment.
verdicts.action: Keep. Only caveat: the Bash egress/write denylists are honestly documented as best-effort tripwires (enforce_manifest.py:75-96) — the REAL egress control (sandbox network policy / egress-allowlist proxy) is named but NOT implemented anywhere in-repo. Ship the runtime sandbox so a Bash-capable agent genuinely cannot exfiltrate; until then blast-radius on egress is unproven.

verdicts.why: Correctly names the provider (Anthropic Claude), versions the disclosure to force re-consent on material change, is revocable, and is genuinely wired into the real entry points (frontdoor.py:301, orchestrator.py:140/264, research.py:65, onboarding.py:80, approvals.py:149). This is one of the few controls that is both built AND consumed. Meets the regulatory bar it targets.
verdicts.action: None required. Minor: the DB connection string is parsed at import from .env.local with no failure handling (consent.py:28-29) — a malformed env would crash import; harden if you want import-time robustness.

verdicts.why: The hash-pin/expiry/consume logic is sound, but it is a parallel, disconnected approval world: approvals live as JSON files under approvals/ (not the tamper-evident audit chain, not the DB), read-modify-write with no locking (TOCTOU on concurrent check/consume), and the actual user-facing approval path — console /api/approvals/decide → approvals.decide() (console.py:452, approvals.py:198) — is a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT mechanism that does NOT hash-pin anything: it just flips a status and re-launches a build. So the strong hash-pinned gate a skeptic would want is not the one the CEO actually clicks.
verdicts.action: Unify: make the console approve button create/approve a verify_approval record whose payload_hash pins the EXACT action to be taken, persist approvals in the DB + audit chain (not loose JSON files), and add row-level locking on consume. approvals.decide must call the hash-pinned verifier, not bypass it.

missing: A wired production-DEPLOY gate. The can_deploy capability and approval_required_for:['deploy'] exist, but there is NO deploy action site in the codebase that calls governance.enforce('deploy') or require_approval before shipping to prod — the entire 'deploys need approval' story gates nothing (grep for deploy action sites returns only voice_guard regex and comments).

Real-dollar spend visibility and forecast at the decision moment. Budgets are token integers; appguard revenue is hardcoded $0. A CEO handling 'millions of dollars of business' is never shown 'this action will cost ~$X, you have $Y of $Z left, projected burn $W/day' before approving.

'Why did the AI do X' explainability tied to the audit chain. audit_log stores actor/action/decision but no human-readable causal rationale, no parent-decision linkage, and nothing surfaces a plain-English 'the agent chose this because…' trail to the CEO. Trust for skeptics REQUIRES this and it is absent.

A runtime network sandbox. enforce_manifest explicitly says the regex egress denylist is a tripwire and 'the REAL control is the runtime sandbox network policy' — which is not implemented. A Bash-capable agent's exfiltration blast-radius is therefore unbounded in practice.

External anchoring / independent verifiability of the audit chain (WORM store, transparency log, or asymmetric signatures + published head hash). Today integrity is provable only to someone holding the same secret that could forge it.
Scheduled enforcement runners: appguard.guard() and audit.verify() both exist but neither is on any schedule — the circuit-breaker and the tamper detector are dormant in the live system.

Spend-velocity anomaly detection / rate limiting. Nothing detects an agent suddenly 10x-ing its burn or looping; the only backstop is a static cap that (a) fails open and (b) whose enforcer isn't scheduled.

Per-tenant audit-key isolation and secret rotation. One global HMAC key protects all tenants' audit history; compromise of one box compromises everyone's tamper-evidence, and there is no rotation path.
churn_moments: CEO is told 'nothing risky happens without your approval' (console approvals subtitle), then learns the hash-pinned approval gate (require_approval) is called by nothing and 'deploy' approval gates no actual deploy — the promise is theater.
A profitable production app gets auto-paused as a 'bleeder' because revenue is hardcoded $0 in the profit math — the CEO watches their best product get a 'we paused this app' page for making money.

…except it wouldn't even pause, because the appguard sweep is on no schedule — so in the OTHER failure mode a runaway app quietly bleeds money for hours because the circuit-breaker never runs until someone manually invokes it.

A skeptical auditor asks 'prove this audit log wasn't edited' and the honest answer is 'trust the secret in the .env file that every agent process can also read' — the tamper-evidence collapses under one pointed question.
The budgets DB hiccups for 30 seconds and the token cap silently disappears (fail-open), so the one moment the governor was needed it waved everything through.

CEO asks 'why did my agent do that?' and the system can show WHAT happened (audit rows) but not WHY — no rationale, no causal chain — which reads as an opaque black box exactly when trust is being decided.

full.domain: Quality engine — scripts/qa/* (story_gen, qa_explorer, dev_loop, qa_run, qa_report), dogfood.py, findings.py, selftest.sh guards, docs/STANDARDS-*.md, and the actual ship gates (factory.py QA, gate_check.py, loopcontroller TESTQA)

verdicts.mechanism: Wiring: is the agentic qa/ stack a mandatory gate on fleet builds?
verdicts.why: It is standalone dead weight. Zero callers exist outside scripts/qa/: grep across scripts/, tests/, platform/ finds no import of qa_run/qa_explorer/dev_loop/story_gen/qa_report. The name collision is damning — factory.py:1474 defines a LOCAL lambda `qa_run` (pytest/node-tests/smoke) that shadows the real engine, so the ship path never touches it. loopcontroller.py:964 gates DELIVER on verify.verify(rigor=2) (tests + static grep security — the adversarial tier only exists at rigor 3, never used on the customer path). scheduler.py:43-54 schedules no QA job. Runtime evidence: /tmp/aos-qa contains only 'console-smoke' reports (agent-os testing its own console today); audit shows RestartTarget=0, DevSelfQA=7, FixBugAttempt=7 — the engine has NEVER run against a fleet-shipped product build.
verdicts.action: Build instead: make qa_run() the producer of the LAUNCH artifact. loopcontroller TESTQA and factory's QA stage must call qa_run(target_url, vision, ...) on the running build; gate_check must consume its machine-readable JSON verdict (report['passed'], blocking_open==0), not a prose file. No build reaches DELIVER without a clean agentic round. Delete the shadowing local lambda name in factory.py.

verdicts.mechanism: Factory ship-gate QA (run_tests / run_js_tests / run_web_qa / run_ext_qa) — what actually gates every shipped build
verdicts.why: The builder grades its own homework: run_tests (factory.py:987) and run_js_tests (factory.py:1035) execute tests the BUILDER wrote — STANDARDS-verification.md rule 5 ('no agent grades its own homework') is violated by the primary gate itself. run_web_qa (factory.py:1058-1091) = 'loads in headless browser without console errors + screenshot' — a smoke-load the verification standard itself calls theatre. run_ext_qa (factory.py:1094) is admittedly static-only ('does not exercise runtime behaviour'). No journey coverage, no expected-vs-actual against the vision, no human-pace/dwell, no story enumeration — for products sold to paying CEOs.
verdicts.action: Replace the QA stage's verification body with the agentic stack: story_gen coverage set from the product charter, qa_explorer runs against the served build, dev_loop fixes blocking bugs, gate on the grounded verdict. Keep builder tests as a fast pre-gate, never as the gate.

verdicts.why: The 'no launch without QA' gate parses PROSE: _v_qa (gate_check.py:~116-135) checks QA-REPORT.md contains the string 'recommend: launch' and no ❌ — any agent that writes those words passes. Worse, controller.py:199-216 _seed() writes gate_check's OWN golden passing artifacts (gate_check._REAL_QA) into every product repo at run start — the gate is satisfied by a canned passing QA report the platform seeds for itself, so selftest.sh's 'gate_check blocks LAUNCH w/o QA' check (selftest.sh:83) proves nothing about real builds.
verdicts.action: Bind the gate to machine-verifiable evidence: gate on qa_report's JSON (passed=true, blocking_open=0, stories>0) written by an actual qa_run execution, hash-linked to the run's screenshots/records and signed by the QA actor (identity.py exists). Kill _v_qa string matching and the golden-artifact seeding on real products.

verdicts.why: The best-engineered piece in the domain: the blame contract (qa_explorer.py:543), retry-on-miss (625-634), settle/re-observe race guard (642-654), and label-over-idx targeting are real anti-false-positive engineering with pinned selftests. But: (1) it violates the repo's OWN REQUIRED standard — STANDARDS-qa.md mandates human-pace typing + 8-12s idle dwell 'for every verification step'; browser_bridge.js contains zero delay/dwell/pressSequentially code, so the leaked-timer bug class that motivated the standard sails straight through the flagship explorer; (2) throughput: the real smoke report shows 3 steps took 5m53s (~2min/step, 2 full CLI agent spawns per step) with stories run strictly serially in qa_run._run_round — an 'exhaustive' 40-story run is days, with no wall-clock or cost budget anywhere; (3) qa_explorer.py:44 hardcodes NODE_PATH to ~/projects/products/noupload/node_modules — the QA engine parasitizes one product's playwright install.
verdicts.action: Add dwell/human-pace verbs to the bridge and make the decide-prompt schedule them per STANDARDS-qa.md; parallelize stories across explorer instances; add a run budget (wall-clock + $) with graceful triage; give the bridge its own pinned playwright dependency.

verdicts.why: 'Complete coverage — not a sample' is one LLM completion (story_gen.py:191). A single reply physically caps at a few dozen stories for an arbitrarily complex product. The iterative-expansion hook (`existing` param, line 168) has ZERO callers. No coverage set is persisted, versioned, or traced to spec acceptance criteria; there is no coverage measure at all, so nobody can ever say what fraction of the product was exercised. On agent failure it returns [] and qa_run proceeds to a 0-story run (qa_report at least says NO VERDICT).
verdicts.action: Make enumeration a loop: generate → self-critique for gaps per surface/persona/category → expand via `existing` until a coverage-judge call says saturated; persist the story corpus per product in Postgres so it grows across releases and fixed bugs pin permanent regression stories.

verdicts.why: The judge is systematically fed fabricated evidence. (1) qa_run.py:239 calls fix_bug WITHOUT target_url/stories/restart_cmd, so residual=[] always, and the judge prompt (dev_loop.py:262-263) explicitly says 'empty means the story now passes' — the principal-engineer judge confirms fixes with zero fresh observation. (2) 'FILES CHANGED by the dev agents' (dev_loop.py:261) is the PLAN's file list, never verified — factory._changed_paths exists and is unused; _spawn_fix_agents (dev_loop.py:225-227) discards factory.agent's return entirely, so a crashed/refused dev agent is indistinguishable from a successful fix. (3) restart_target's pkill -f on argv[-1] (dev_loop.py:105) can kill unrelated processes ('npm start' → pkill -f npm). (4) dev_self_qa — the owner-mandated 'dev is the first QA' — has zero callers in the fleet; no builder ever self-QAs before handoff. That mandate is fiction.
verdicts.action: Build instead: fix_bug must always restart + re-explore the failing story (make target_url/stories mandatory), judge on a real git diff of changed files, fail an attempt when a spawned agent returns rc!=0, and pkill by tracked PID not pattern. Wire dev_self_qa into factory's BUILD stage as a hard pre-handoff gate.

verdicts.why: The loop shape (rounds, fix-and-rerun-all, early stop on blocking) is right, and the offline selftest genuinely pins the state machine. But it contradicts the north star by design: a 'clean' round means no BLOCKING bug (qa_run.py:222) — non-blocking bugs are 'noted' in a /tmp markdown file and shipped ('ship-with-known-issues is a real, honest outcome', qa_report.py:95) with NO findings.py filing, so every non-blocking bug reaches a human by architecture. Reports and screenshots live only in /tmp/aos-qa (qa_report.py OUT_DIR) — a reboot erases all QA history. report['passed'] gates nothing. No round/wall-clock budget accounting is surfaced to anyone.
verdicts.action: On clean-with-open-bugs, file every open bug through findings.py (routed owner, SLA) instead of a /tmp note; persist runs to Postgres + object store; emit the verdict to the gate and to the CEO's quality view; treat 'zero open bugs' — not 'zero blocking' — as the ship bar, with an explicit governed override for known-issue ships.

verdicts.why: ~110 checks of impressive breadth, but grep 'qa' over selftest.sh returns NOTHING: not one of the five scripts/qa/* selftests is registered, and tests/test_core.py doesn't import them either — the quality engine is the only subsystem with no guard, so a regression in the explorer/blame-contract ships silently. Worse, the guard corrupts production state: dogfood.py's selftest (run by selftest.sh:179) calls run_once with a stubbed agent but REAL audit.append (dogfood.py:111), so every selftest.sh run writes a fake DogfoodPass row — the DB shows 13 DogfoodPass rows, ALL persona=first-run, ALL found=1/filed=1 (the stub's canned values), which both fakes acceptance-coverage history and breaks _next_persona rotation (keyed on that same audit count, dogfood.py:62-69). Also there is no git repo and no CI hook — nothing forces selftest.sh to run before a change lands.
verdicts.action: Register all five qa/* selftests as ckp lines; make dogfood._selftest stub audit.append (or tag selftest audit rows and exclude them from count); put agent-os under version control with selftest.sh as a mandatory pre-merge hook.

verdicts.mechanism: dogfood.py — the standing demanding-user acceptance pass
verdicts.why: The 'astonish a skeptic' lens runs WEEKLY (scheduler.py:53, 604800s) with ONE persona per tick — a full 9-persona rotation takes 9 weeks, for users who churn at one frustration. The 'demanding user' never opens a browser: the prompt tells a 'research-growth' agent to 'curl the HTML/JSON routes' (dogfood.py:83-84) — judging a SPA's UX, latency, and rendering by curling HTML, while a full browser-driving explorer sits unused one directory away. Blocker severity is silently downgraded to 'high' (dogfood.py:104). And the production evidence says it has never worked: findings table has 0 rows ever (all 75 FindingFiled audit rows are self-cleaning selftests), and every recorded DogfoodPass is the selftest stub.
verdicts.action: Build instead: daily (or per-deploy) multi-persona pass that drives the LIVE console through qa_explorer with the persona brief as the vision, on real journeys (signup→build→wait→review→pay), filing every finding with true severity; alert the fleet on any blocker within minutes, not weeks.

verdicts.why: The routing spine is genuinely good (owner via directory, taskboard visibility, SLA sweep, audit). But closure is on the honor system: resolve() (findings.py:86-94) flips status on any caller's say-so with zero verification — no re-run of the failing scenario, no evidence requirement, directly violating STANDARDS-verification.md rule 6 ('reproduce the exact complaint, re-run the original repro after the fix'). sweep() (findings.py:108-121) only sends a notification on SLA breach — no escalation ladder, no re-route, no CEO-visible aging. And in production it has processed zero real findings — the whole loop is selftested but unexercised.
verdicts.action: Gate resolve() on a verification artifact: re-run the originating story/persona check and require a passing record id before status='resolved'; escalate overdue findings by re-routing to a senior role and surfacing on the cockpit, not just an ntfy ping.

verdicts.why: The standards are excellent diagnoses — and largely unenforced (the repo's own documented 'declared-not-wired' bug class). STANDARDS-verification.md names 'scripts/test_artifact_review.py (and the growing seeded e2e)' as THE standing gate — that file does not exist anywhere in the repo. missing: A mandatory pre-ship invocation of the agentic QA on EVERY fleet build — the single most important wire in the domain does not exist; today's real gates are builder-authored tests + a console-error smoke-load.

Production error telemetry loop: no crash/error capture from live tenant products feeding findings.py — 'zero bugs reach a human' requires catching what QA missed in prod before the user notices; nothing exists (no Sentry-equivalent, no client error beacon, no log-anomaly → finding).

Persistent regression corpus: stories are regenerated from scratch each run and fixed bugs pin no permanent regression test; a bug fixed in round 2 can silently return next release with no memory of it.
Verifier-of-the-verifier for the agentic stack: STANDARDS-verification.md rule 5 demands an independent agent audit every green; qa_run's greens are audited by no one.
Version control + CI: /home/swami/projects/agent-os is not a git repo and nothing forces selftest.sh (or the qa/* selftests) to run on change — 'dev self-tests exhaustively' has no trigger.

Human-pace/dwell capability in the QA browser bridge (typing delays, 8-12s idle assertions, session-expiry transits) — the documented bug class that reached the owner remains structurally invisible to every product QA path.

Non-functional QA on shipped products: no latency/SLO budget checks, no load beyond factory's 200-request /health probe, no accessibility or mobile-viewport pass, no data-durability (restart round-trip) checks in the agentic engine.

Cross-story/exploratory security QA on the running product (auth bypass, tenant isolation, IDOR) — 'qa-security' is a role name; the explorer's prompts mention security but no story category or check enforces it.
QA visibility to the CEO-user: run reports live in /tmp with no console surface, so the paying CEO can never see WHAT was tested on their product — fatal for skeptics who trust AI less than humans.
Cost/duration accounting and parallelism for QA runs: 2 agent spawns per step, serial stories, no budget — 'exhaustive' is economically and temporally undefined.
full.headline: You built a genuinely clever self-testing QA robot and then never plugged it into the assembly line — every product we ship is still approved by the builder grading its own tests against a launch report the platform seeds for itself, and the weekly 'demanding user' has never filed a single real finding.
churn_moments: A CEO's first shipped product passes 'QA' (its own builder-written node tests + a renders-without-console-errors smoke) and their first real customer clicks a dead button the idle explorer would have caught — the flagship QA engine has run only against agent-os's own console smoke, never a tenant build.

The CEO opens docs/QA-REPORT.md to check what was verified before LAUNCH and a diligent one discovers it's the platform's own canned golden artifact (controller.py _seed writes gate_check._REAL_QA) — instant, unrecoverable trust collapse for a user who already trusts AI less than humans.

The CEO pauses mid-typing on a form in their shipped product and a leaked timer bounces them — the exact bug class STANDARDS-qa.md documents as having reached the owner, still untestable because no product QA path types at human pace or dwells.

QA declares a round 'clean' with three non-blocking bugs 'noted' in a /tmp markdown file nobody reads or routes — the CEO is the one who finds all three, violating the core promise in the north star's own words.

A blocking bug is 'fixed': the judge was told residual=[] ('empty means the story now passes') without any re-observation and 'FILES CHANGED' was the plan's wish-list — the CEO re-hits the same bug an hour later and watches the system claim it was fixed.

A frustrated user churns on Monday over an onboarding dead-end; the acceptance dogfood pass that would flag it runs the following week, as a curl-based text audit, under a persona rotation that is stuck on 'first-run' because the selftest polluted the audit counter.
